## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/abut-integral — Abutment type: conventional / integral / semi-integral (input panel I-0a, Tab 10) (PR link added after merge)

**What:** new abutment-type selector (IAB) with the design of integral and semi-integral abutments per owner. Conventional cantilever stays the default and the existing design (Tabs 1–9) is unchanged.

- **Panel I-0a "Abutment Type"** (Geometry input tab, after I-0): conventional / integral / semi-integral, with the inputs of the chosen type (bridge geometry for eligibility, integral cap and diaphragm, movement and earth pressure, piles, bars).
- **Eligibility and owner rules** on the Owner Requirements card (Tab 1 §1.0a), listed only for the chosen type (rule flag `iab`): MassDOT Part I 3.10.11.1 simplified-method boundary conditions (length 140/200 ft, skew 30°, straight/curvature 5°, grade 5 %, height 15 ft, parallel abutments, U-wings, rock below tip and not scour susceptible), 3.10.10.1 (HP10X57 / HP12X84 Gr 50, webs parallel to the abutment), 3.10.10.3 (spacing 3'-6"–10 ft, a pile per beam line, flange to end 18 in–3 ft, 2 ft embedment), 3.10.11.2 (L ≥ L_f + 5 ft), 3.10.2 / 3.10.8 load rules, 3.10.8 connection bars and fill cover, 3.1.8.3 joint, 3.4.6.1 (semi-integral seismic note); RIDOT 11.3.2 (skew, length, deck to bottom of cap 13 ft, cap depth 3.5–6 ft, grade, straight, girder 6 ft, pile 10 ft, weak axis, 2 ft embedment, p-y design, IM / γTU / at-rest below 0.5 in, pre-augering, joint at ½ in), 11.3.3 (skew, expansion length 175/300 ft, grade, girder depth, full passive, independent wings, both ends semi-integral, spread or multiple pile rows); CTDOT V2 App. CT11.1.1.1 (skew < 30°, length 150/200 ft, span 150 ft, height 12 ft, end heights within 1 ft, Gr 50 H-piles b_f ≥ 10 in weak axis, 10 ft below the stem, 2 ft embedment, U-wings), CT11.1.1.4.2a (stem 3.5 ft wide, 4 ft below grade), CT11.1.1.3 load rules, 11.6.1.3.1CT (semi-integral pinned, lower portion a standard cantilever); AASHTO (owner AASHTO, now also listed): 11.6.1.3 / C11.6.1.3 (no numeric limits), C3.11.1, 10.7.1.2, p-y moment. For an integral abutment the rules of the conventional cantilever (footing, stem, backwall) are not listed; the screening advisories "int"/"semi" are listed only for a conventional abutment.
- **Thermal movement** (Tab 10 §10.2): Δ = γTU·α·ΔT·L_exp, γTU = 1.00, L_exp = L_tot/2 (or entered), α and ΔT from panel I-6b (owner defaults there), CTDOT integral: 150 °F range −30/+120 °F about the setting temperature (default 50 °F).
- **Earth pressure from the wall movement** (§10.3), expansion and contraction: MassDOT 3.10.8 K = 0.43 + 5.7[1 − exp(−190 δT/H)]; CTDOT Eq. CT11.1.1.3-1 Rankine K_p (contraction: no soil pressure, CT11.1.1.4.2a); RIDOT 11.3.2 K_0 when Δ_exp < 0.5 in else K_p, 11.3.3 full K_p; AASHTO C3.11.1 / Table C3.11.1-1: K = K_0 + (K_p − K_0)·min(1, (Δ/H)/(Δ/H)_p); contraction (all but CTDOT integral) K = K_0 − (K_0 − K_a)·min(1, (Δ/H)/(Δ/H)_a). K_p Rankine unless entered. H = deck surface to bottom of cap (integral) or of the end diaphragm (semi-integral, = h_bw).
- **Integral piles** (§10.4): gravity per pile at Strength I (DL equally; LL equally without IM for MassDOT, LL+IM with the rigid-cap eccentricity otherwise). MassDOT simplified method: P_u from Tables 3.10.11-2/-3 by soil type, interpolated on skew; L_f, L_e. CTDOT closed form CT11.1.1.3-2 and CT11.1.1.4.2c-2 to -9: Δ_L, M_T, F_T (fixed or pinned head), θ_W, M_W, R_T; P_u = P_g + R_T, M_u = min(M_p, M_T + M_W); AASHTO 6.9.2.2.1 interaction with φc = 0.70, φf = 1.00 (6.5.4.2), P_n = F_y·A_s (fully braced), M_n,y = min(F_yZ_y, 1.6F_yS_y) with the 6.12.2.2.1c FLB check. RIDOT / AASHTO: the same interaction with the pile-head moment entered from a p-y analysis (Pile Designer, integral mode); not complete until entered.
- **Cap and wall** (§10.5): case 1 cap a continuous beam on the piles for all vertical loads, M_u = 0.8·w_u·s²/8, V_u = w_u·s/2 (MassDOT 3.10.8, CTDOT CT11.1.1.4.2a); case 2 whole wall a horizontal beam on the girders under the expansion pressure at its base, same 0.8 rule, largest girder spacing; rear face of the cap a cantilever from the seat under the expansion pressure (CTDOT design case 1). Semi-integral: the end diaphragm (backwall inputs) as case 2; its force to the superstructure reported. Section checks: the abutment's sectionCheck (general shear procedure, no stirrups).
- **Stability basis** (§10.6): integral — no sliding / eccentricity / bearing check (restrained by the superstructure strut, single row of piles); checked instead: piles, pile length, cap and wall. Semi-integral — lower abutment = conventional Tabs 3–5 (pinned connection, bearing shear).
- **Dashboard:** integral keeps only the wing checks of the conventional list and adds iabPile, iabTip (MassDOT), iabC1/C2/C3 (F, V, Min); semi-integral drops the four bw* backwall checks and adds iabD (F, V, Min). Tabs 2–8 carry a note for an integral abutment; Tab 5 a note for semi-integral. Report: Tab 10 section, IAB references, input echo; for an integral abutment the conventional sections (Tabs 2–6, 8, 3D) are left out and the key results are the integral ones.
- **Graphics:** integral section (diaphragm, cap, girder, pile with embedment, MassDOT crushed-stone trench, approach slab, pressure triangle, dimensions) and semi-integral section (stem, footing, bearing, moving end diaphragm and joint), SVG in Tab 10 §10.0.

**Saved data (CLAUDE.md §5):** new object `S.iab` (type, b, hc, hd, dg, grade, curve, dH, Dfront, straight, parallel, rockBelow, noScour, bothEnds, Lexp, Tset, epsSH, bfType, KpUser, gEH, qApp, sec, Fy, n, sp, orient, embed, Lpile, soilMD, head, LE, EG, IG, MuPy, capBar, capSp, hBar, hSp, vBar, vSp). `type` defaults to "conv" for new projects and for saved projects without it (`migrate()` creates it; missing fields take defaults). No existing key or format changed. With type "conv" the Input ID is unchanged (`fpS.iab` dropped from the fingerprint).

**Result change (CLAUDE.md §4):** none for a conventional abutment (verified, below). New calculations only for integral / semi-integral.

**Where:** `iabDefault`, `IAB_MD`, `IAB_PUB`, `iabSect`, `IAB_BF`, `iabType` (Section A, after `wingDefault`); `defaultState` key `iab`; owner rules `OWN_LK_IAB` … `ABUT_OWN.rules.push(` (before `abutOwnChecks`) and the filter in `abutOwnChecks` (anchor `const it=iabType();`); `ownerPanelHTML` (AASHTO card with rows); `VALID` entries `iab.*`; `ABUT_IN_SEC` `'in-iab'`; `buildInputs` panel `I-0a Abutment type`; `computeIAB` (Section C, after `computeWing`); `computeAll` anchor `C-11e Integral / semi-integral`, dashboard block `if(R.iab){` before `R.dash=dash;`, fingerprint `if(fpS.iab&&`; `migrate` anchor `IAB (2026-10-20): a project saved before`; `renderTabIAB`, `svgIabSection`, `DASH_ANCHOR` (iab*); `TABS`, `ABUT_TABNAME`, `TAB_RENDER`, `renderTabContent` (notes); change handler string paths; `inputEchoHTML`, `IAB_REFS`, `buildReport` (key results, secNames, SKIP, 3D, result-block regex).

**Check case 1 — MassDOT integral (built-in project: L_ab = 44 ft, 6 girders @ 8 ft, DC/DW/LL+IM = 85/12/70 kip per girder; φ = 32°, γ = 0.120 kcf; owner MassDOT, steel, L_tot = 120 ft, skew 0; b = 3.5, h_c = 4, h_d = 5 ft; 6 HP12X84 @ 8 ft, soil type 3, pile 30 ft):**
δT = 6.5×10⁻⁶ (70)(60×12) = 0.3276 in; δT/H = 0.3276/108 = 0.003033; K = 0.43 + 5.7[1 − e^(−0.5763)] = 2.927; P_exp = ½(2.927)(0.120)(9)² = 14.22 kip/ft.
Pile: DC = 510 + 0.150(3.5)(9)(44) = 717.9 kip; P_DL = (1.25·717.9 + 1.50·72)/6 = 167.56 kip; LL without IM = 420/1.33 = 315.8 kip → P_LL = 1.75(315.8)/6 = 92.11 kip; P_g = 259.67 kip vs Table 3.10.11-3 (dense dry sand, 0°) 561 kip → D/C 0.463; L_f + 5 = 27 ft vs 30 ft → 0.90.
Case 2: p = 2.927(0.120)(9) = 3.161 ksf; w_u = 1.35(3.161) = 4.267 kip/ft; M_u = 0.8(4.267)(8)²/8 = 27.31 kip-ft/ft. Rear face: M = (2.927·0.120)[(9³ − 5³)/3 − 5(9² − 5²)/2] = 21.54 kip-ft/ft.
(Before: no integral design existed.) Tool values identical.

**Check case 2 — CTDOT integral (same project; owner CTDOT: φ = 35°, γ = 0.125, α = 6.4×10⁻⁶; T_set = 50 °F; fixed head, L_E = 10 ft, E_G = 29,000 ksi, I_G = 60,000 in⁴):**
K_p = tan²(62.5°) = 3.690; Δ_L = 0.6(6.4×10⁻⁶·80 + 500×10⁻⁶)(1440/2) = 0.4372 in; EI = 29,000(213) = 6.177×10⁶ kip-in²; M_T = min(2660, 6EIΔ/L_E²) = 1125 kip-in; F_T = 12EIΔ/L_E³ = 18.75 kip; P_g = 167.56 + 1.75(420)/6 = 290.06 kip; W = 2(6)(290.06)/6 = 580.1 kip; θ_W = 580.1(960)²/(24·29,000·60,000) = 0.01280 rad; M_W = 4EIθ/L_E = 2636 kip-in; P_P = 1.35(½·3.690·0.125·9²·44)/6 = 184.95 kip; R_T = (184.95·72 + 18.75·108 + 1125)/960 = 17.15 kip; P_u = 307.22 kip, M_u = min(2660, 3761) = 2660 kip-in; P_r = 0.70(50)(24.6) = 861 kip; 307.22/861 + (8/9)(2660/2660) = 1.246 → FAIL (the end-rotation moment of the soft default I_G governs; input-driven). Tool values identical.

**Check case 3 — AASHTO semi-integral (built-in project, steel, L_exp = span/2 = 40 ft, ΔT_rise 52 °F, h_bw = 5 ft, dense sand):** Δ = 6.5×10⁻⁶(52)(480) = 0.1622 in; Δ/H = 0.002704; K = 0.470 + (3.255 − 0.470)(0.2704) = 1.223; p = 1.223(0.120)(5) = 0.734 ksf; M_u = 0.8(1.35·0.734)(8)²/8 = 6.34 kip-ft/ft; #6 @ 9, t_bw = 18 in: φM_n = 40.11 → D/C 0.158. Tool values identical.

**How verified:** `node tests/check-syntax.mjs abutment_calculator.html` (all scripts pass). Headless (Playwright, tests/lib.mjs), origin/main vs branch, conventional type: built-in project, MassDOT, RIDOT on piles with ADT, CTDOT with Extreme Event I, AASHTO on piles with 20° skew, and an old save without `iab` and `wing` — Input ID, the whole computeAll() result (every value except the new `R.iab`), the warnings and the rendered text of Tabs 1–5, 8 and 9 identical (self-test time stamp masked). Integral (MassDOT, CTDOT, RIDOT with p-y moment, AASHTO) and semi-integral (RIDOT, AASHTO, MassDOT) run without page errors; every TeX line of Tab 10 and Tab 1 rendered with KaTeX (no errors); the report builds for all types. Check cases 1–3 reproduced in Python from the formulas above.

**Other copies:** none (Pile Designer.html holds the same MassDOT table data; not edited, no hand-off added).

**Open items (engineer decision):**
1. γ_EH on the movement-induced (toward-passive) pressure: Table 3.4.1-2 has no passive row; default 1.35 (the at-rest maximum), editable.
2. AASHTO owner: K between K_0 and K_p (expansion) and between K_0 and K_a (contraction) interpolated linearly in Δ/H against Table C3.11.1-1 — AASHTO gives the end points only.
3. CTDOT: setting temperature for the 150 °F integral range (default 50 °F, the BRSDM median for bearings and joints); R_DL+LL in θ_W taken factored (as RIDOT 11.3.2); M_T and M_W added; passive force per pile factored by γ_EH; Δ_L from the fall (the "negative differential").
4. Semi-integral end diaphragm: MassDOT 3.10.8 K and CTDOT K_p (both written for integral abutments) applied to it.
5. Semi-integral lower stem keeps the full-height earth pressure of Tab 1 §1.3 (conservative: the diaphragm's soil goes to the superstructure).
6. γTU = 1.00 on the movement for AASHTO (MassDOT and RIDOT state 1.00 for integral abutments).
7. Cap shear (case 1) without stirrups (general procedure): the built-in project fails case 1 shear (D/C 1.70); stirrup shear V_s is not modelled.
8. MassDOT pile end distance and all spacings measured along the abutment as entered (the manual measures along the skew).

**Diff (exact before/after, `git diff -U0`):**

+    Dfront:4.0,                            // bottom of the cap below the finished grade at the front face (ft)
+    straight:true, parallel:true, rockBelow:true, noScour:true, bothEnds:true,   // straight girders / alignment; parallel abutments and piers; top of rock below the pile tip; not scour susceptible; both ends semi-integral
+    Lexp:0, Tset:50, epsSH:0.0005,         // expansion length to this abutment (ft, 0 = half the total length); CTDOT integral setting temperature (°F); CTDOT shrinkage strain
+    bfType:"dense", KpUser:0, gEH:1.35, qApp:0,   // backfill for Table C3.11.1-1; K_p entered (0 = Rankine); γEH on the movement-induced pressure; approach-slab dead load on the abutment (kip/ft)
+    sec:"HP12X84", Fy:50, n:6, sp:8.0, orient:"weak", embed:24, Lpile:30,     // piles: section, F_y (ksi), number (single row), spacing (ft), "weak" (web parallel to the abutment CL) | "strong", embedment into the cap (in), length below the cap (ft)
+    soilMD:3, head:"fixed", LE:10.0, EG:29000, IG:60000, MuPy:0,              // MassDOT soil type (Table 3.10.11-1); CTDOT head condition, equivalent cantilever L_E (ft), girder E (ksi) and composite I (in^4); pile-head moment from a p-y analysis (kip-ft, 0 = not entered)

+}
+// MassDOT Bridge Manual Part I Tables 3.10.11-2 (HP10X57) and 3.10.11-3 (HP12X84): factored axial load per pile P_u (kip) at skew 0/10/20/30°
+// and depth to fixity L_f (ft); Table 3.10.11-4: equivalent length L_e (ft); soil types of Table 3.10.11-1 (same data as Pile Designer.html)
+const IAB_MD={soils:["Dry loose sand","Wet loose sand","Dry dense sand","Wet dense sand","Wet stiff clay","Wet soft clay"],
+  HP10X57:{Pu:[[420,378,342,312],[429,390,356,330],[367,295,242,203],[378,312,263,226],[380,296,248,214],[471,428,403,385]], Lf:[26,28,19,20,16,26], Le:[8.3,8.5,7.3,7.5,7.5,10]},
+  HP12X84:{Pu:[[641,586,538,500],[654,603,560,525],[561,461,389,336],[580,488,423,374],[583,468,405,361],[713,657,625,603]], Lf:[31,32,22,23,18,30], Le:[9.5,9.8,8.3,8.5,8.5,11.5]}};
+// published AISC properties of the two MassDOT sections (as in Pile Designer.html); other HP shapes from flange and web rectangles (fillets neglected)
+const IAB_PUB={HP10X57:{Ix:294,Sx:58.8,Zx:66.5,Iy:101,Sy:19.7,Zy:30.3}, HP12X84:{Ix:650,Sx:106,Zx:120,Iy:213,Sy:34.6,Zy:53.2}};
+function iabSect(k){ const h=HP_SHAPES[k]||HP_SHAPES.HP12X84, [A,d,bf,tf,tw]=h, hw=d-2*tf, P=IAB_PUB[k];

+    b+=`<rect x="${X(-7)}" y="${Y(0)}" width="${(7+0.4)*sc}" height="${Math.max(0.3,+I.dg)*sc}" fill="none" stroke="#1f3a5f" stroke-dasharray="5 3"/>`+svgT(X(-6.8),Y(Math.max(0.3,+I.dg))-5,"girder (cast into the diaphragm)",{fs:10,c:"#1f3a5f"});
+    b+=`<rect x="${X(0)}" y="${Y(-0.7)}" width="${bw*sc}" height="${(hd+0.7)*sc}" fill="#ecebe4" stroke="#333" stroke-width="1.4"/>`+svgT(X(bw/2),Y(hd/2),"end diaphragm",{fs:10,a:"middle"});
+    b+=`<rect x="${X(0)}" y="${Y(hd)}" width="${bw*sc}" height="${hc*sc}" fill="#e4e2d8" stroke="#333" stroke-width="1.4"/>`+svgT(X(bw/2),Y(hd+0.9),"pile cap",{fs:10,a:"middle"});
+    b+=`<line x1="${X(0)}" y1="${Y(hd)}" x2="${X(bw)}" y2="${Y(hd)}" stroke="#777" stroke-dasharray="3 3"/>`+svgT(X(-0.2),Y(hd)+4,"seat",{fs:9.5,a:"end",c:"#666"});

## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/abut-integral-2 — Integral / semi-integral follow-up: nonlinear mobilization, semi-integral lower-stem pressure, cap stirrups, skew definitions (PR link added after merge)

Engineer decisions on the open items of the IAB entry above (items 2, 5, 7, 8; items 1, 3, 4, 6 kept as they are).

### F-IAB2-1. Earth-pressure mobilization between at-rest and the limit state: hyperbolic, not linear   [calc change] [integral / semi-integral only]
- **Where:** Section A, new `IAB_RF`, `iabHyp` (anchor `IAB2 (2026-10-20): mobilization`); `computeIAB` anchors `Q.kM="aashto"` and `Q.kC="aashto"`; `renderTabIAB` §10.3 lines and notes.
- **Before:** `Q.fP=Math.min(1,Q.rE/bf.p); Q.Kexp=K0+(Kp-K0)*Q.fP;` and `Q.fA=Math.min(1,Q.rC/bf.a); Q.Kcon=K0-(K0-Ka)*Q.fA;` (linear in Δ/H).
- **After:** `Q.xP=Math.min(1,Q.rE/bf.p); Q.fP=iabHyp(Q.xP); Q.Kexp=K0+(Kp-K0)*Q.fP;` and `Q.xA=Math.min(1,Q.rC/bf.a); Q.fA=iabHyp(Q.xA); Q.Kcon=K0-(K0-Ka)*Q.fA;` with `iabHyp(x) = x/((1−R_f) + R_f·x)`, R_f = 0.85.
- **Basis:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.11.1 and Table C3.11.1-1 give only the movement that reaches full active / passive pressure. The 10th Ed. has no mobilization curve (searched Sections 3, 10 and 11 and their commentary: no figure or equation). The hyperbolic load–deflection form of Duncan & Mokwa (2001), with failure ratio R_f = 0.85, is used. It is normalized so the limit is reached at the Table C3.11.1-1 Δ/H (x = 1). Applies to the AASHTO-owner expansion K and to the contraction K of every owner except CTDOT integral (CTDOT: no soil pressure in contraction). Less conservative (lower K) than linear at no movement: f(0) = 0 for both. It is more conservative (higher K) at every movement in between.
- **Check case (AASHTO semi-integral, built-in project, Δ = 0.1622 in, h_bw = 5 ft, dense sand, φ = 32°):** x = 0.002704/0.01 = 0.2704. Before: f = 0.2704, K = 0.470 + 2.785(0.2704) = 1.223. After: f = 0.2704/(0.15 + 0.85·0.2704) = 0.7119, K = 0.470 + 2.785(0.7119) = 2.452. Diaphragm M_u = 0.8(1.35·2.452·0.120·5)(8²)/8 = 12.71 kip-ft/ft (before 6.34); D/C 0.158 → 0.317. AASHTO integral (Δ/H = 0.002253): K 1.098 → 2.307, case 2 M_u 10.24 → 21.53 kip-ft/ft.

### F-IAB2-2. Semi-integral: the lower abutment takes the earth pressure below the seat only   [calc change] [semi-integral only; conventional and integral unchanged]
- **Where:** `computeAll` C-3 (anchor `IAB2 (2026-10-20): semi-integral — the pressure on the virtual back plane`), LS (`const hLS=H-hCut`), ES (`const hES=`), M–O (`const PaSumA=` now on `PaFull`), stem demand (`const cS=`, `stEH`, `stLS`, `stQ`, `const cL=`), `buildVM` stem (`const hAbove=`), `stemCapacityProfile`, Tab 1 §1.3 / §1.4 and Tab 5 §5.2 worked lines, Tab 10 §10.0 text.
- **Before:** EH, LS and ES on the lower abutment over the full retained height (conservative).
- **After (semi-integral, not the construction stage):** h_cut = H − (t_f + h_stem) on the virtual back plane; P_a = P_a,full − P_cut, z̄ = (P_a,full·z̄_full − P_cut·z_cut)/P_a; LS and ES over H − h_cut. Stem base, c = h_soil − h_stem: M_EH = k_ah·γ[H³/6 − (Hc²/2 − c³/3)], V_EH = k_ah·γ(H² − c²)/2, M_LS = k_ah·γ·h_eq(H − c)²/2, V_LS = k_ah·γ·h_eq(H − c); the soil above the seat stays as overburden. V&M stem: no pressure above the seat. Construction stage (no superstructure, no diaphragm) and the Extreme Event I M–O increment stay on the full height. Conventional: h_cut = c = 0 and the original expressions are used unchanged (bit-identical).
- **Basis:** statics; CTDOT BRSDM V2 11.6.1.3.1CT, RIDOT BDM 11.3.3: the end diaphragm moves with the superstructure (pinned connection, bearings on the seat), so the soil it retains loads the superstructure and not the lower abutment.
- **Check case (AASHTO semi-integral, built-in: t_f = 3, h_stem = 14, h_soil = 19 ft, k_a = 0.3073, γ = 0.120):** H = 22, h_cut = 5 ft. P_a,full = ½(0.3073)(0.120)(22²) = 8.923 kip/ft; P_cut = ½(0.3073)(0.120)(5²) = 0.461 at z = 22 − 10/3 = 18.667 ft; P_a = 8.462 kip/ft at z̄ = (8.923·7.333 − 0.461·18.667)/8.462 = 6.716 ft (before 8.923 at 7.333). LS_h = 0.07374(17)(44) = 55.16 kip (before 71.38). Stem: c = 5, M_EH = 0.03687[19³/6 − (19·25/2 − 125/3)] = 34.93 kip-ft/ft (before 42.15); V_EH = 0.03687(361 − 25)/2 = 6.194 (6.655); M_LS = 0.03687(2.1)(14²)/2 = 7.588 (13.976). Stem M_u (Strength I) 112.06 → 90.05 kip-ft/ft, D/C 0.370 → 0.298; eccentricity D/C 0.707 → 0.551; bearing 0.933 → 0.861. Sliding 1.153 unchanged: the construction stage governs, and that stage is unchanged.

### F-IAB2-3. Integral pile cap stirrups (case 1 shear)   [calc change] [integral only; default unchanged]
- **Where:** `iabDefault` (`stBar:"0", stLegs:2, stSp:12.0`); panel I-0a (`Cap stirrups (vertical)`, with the note on D/C 1.70); `computeIAB` anchor `IAB2: cap stirrups`; `sectionHTML` (shear block: an extra block and the check use `c.stir` when present; unchanged otherwise); input echo; `VALID["iab.stSp"]`.
- **Before:** concrete only, general procedure, β by Eq. 5.7.3.4.2-2.
- **After (stirrups entered):** A_v = n·A_b; A_v,min = 0.0316√f′c·b_v·s/f_y (Eq. 5.7.2.5-1). If A_v ≥ A_v,min, β = 4.8/(1 + 750ε_s) (Eq. 5.7.3.4.2-1), else Eq. 5.7.3.4.2-2. θ = 29 + 3500ε_s (Eq. 5.7.3.4.2-3); V_s = A_v·f_y·d_v·cot θ/s (Eq. 5.7.3.3-4, α = 90°); φV_n = 0.90·min(V_c + V_s, 0.25f′c·b_v·d_v) (Eqs. 5.7.3.3-1, -2). Per ft of cap width. Default "none": results unchanged (built-in AASHTO project D/C 1.70, noted in the panel).
- **Basis:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 5.7.2.5, 5.7.3.3, 5.7.3.4.2.
- **Check case (MassDOT integral, f′c = 5 ksi, b = 3.5 ft, h_c = 4 ft, #5 × 4 legs @ 6 in):** d_v = 40.95 in, ε_s = 2.960×10⁻³, V_u = 45.20 kip/ft. A_v = 1.24 ≥ A_v,min = 0.0316√5(42)(6)/60 = 0.297 in². β = 4.8/(1 + 2.220) = 1.491; θ = 39.36°. V_c = 0.0316(1.491)√5(12)(40.95) = 51.76; V_s = 1.24(60)(40.95)cot 39.36°/(6·3.5) = 176.88 kip/ft. φV_n = 0.9(228.64) = 205.78 kip/ft. D/C = 0.220 (before, no stirrups: 1.521).

### F-IAB2-4. MassDOT pile spacing and end distance: along the skew   [label / display only] [no result change]
- **Where:** panel I-0a input label and title (`Pile spacing s along the abutment (along the skew)`); MassDOT rule `iab.sp` (value, limit, worked s_n); Tab 10 §10.4 layout lines; case 2 span label.
- **Before / after:** values unchanged. L_ab, the beam positions (panel I-5: "positions along the abutment") and the pile spacing are all measured along the abutment centerline, i.e. along the skew. MassDOT Part I 3.10.10.3 measures the pile flange-to-abutment-end distance along the skew; the tool's end distance is that value. MassDOT gives no measuring direction for the 3'-6" to 10 ft spacing limits, so they are applied to the c/c spacing along the pile row; the spacing normal to the girders s_n = s·cos(skew) is shown for reference. MassDOT 3.10.8 case 2 spans "equal to the girder spacing along the skew" — the beam-position spacing used. The earlier open item 8 ("the manual measures along the skew, the tool along the abutment") was a misreading: the two are the same direction.
- **Check case:** s = 8.00 ft along the skew, skew 20° → s_n = 8 cos 20° = 7.52 ft (display); end distance (22.00 − 20.00)(12) − 12.30/2 = 17.85 in along the skew (unchanged).

### Saved data (§5)
New `S.iab` fields `stBar` ("0"), `stLegs` (2), `stSp` (12). They are filled by `migrate()` for projects saved before this change, through the existing field-by-field fill of `S.iab`. No key or format changed. The conventional Input ID is unchanged: `fpS.iab` is dropped for "conv".

### How verified
- `node tests/check-syntax.mjs abutment_calculator.html`: all scripts pass.
- Headless, origin/main (#373) vs the branch, conventional type. Cases: built-in, MassDOT, RIDOT on piles with ADT, CTDOT with Extreme Event I, AASHTO on piles at 20° skew, an old save without `iab`/`wing`, sloped backfill + water table + ES, and a conventional project carrying stirrup fields. Identical: the Input ID, every pre-existing value of `computeAll()` (new keys only: `EH.PaFull/zEHf/hCut/Pcut/zCut`, `LS.hLS`, `stemDem.cS/cL`), the warnings, and the rendered text of Tabs 1–6, 8 and 9 (self-test time stamp masked).
- Check cases F-IAB2-1 to -3 read from the running tool, before (origin/main) and after, and recomputed by hand.
- Every TeX line of Tabs 1, 5 and 10 renders with KaTeX for integral (MassDOT with stirrups, CTDOT, RIDOT, AASHTO) and semi-integral (RIDOT, AASHTO). The report builds for all types.

### Other copies
None.

### Open items
1. R_f = 0.85 (Duncan & Mokwa 2001) is a tool choice; the AASHTO 10th Ed. gives no curve.
2. Semi-integral construction stage and Extreme Event I increment on the full height (unchanged, conservative).

## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/abut-interactive — Interactive figures (hover / tap values, selectors, click to the worked calculation) (ABINT) (PR link added after merge)

UI only. No formula, factor, unit or code reference changed. `computeAll()` is not edited. The printed calculation report is byte-identical to main (checked below).

### F-ABINT-1. Shared machinery — display only
- **Where:** Section E, after `svgWrap()`, anchor `ABINT (2026-10-20): interactive figures`: `FIG`, `FIG_STATIC`, `FIG_X`, `fia()`, `fg()`, `fF()`, `figInterp()`, `FIG_FN`, `figLsSel()`, `figCtl()`, `figBox()`, `figRedraw()`, `figStaticIn()`, `figCrossDraw()`, `figTipShow()`, `figTipHide()`, `figLink()`, `d3PileHL()`, `figWire()`; CSS anchor `ABINT: interactive figures — selectors`.
- **Before:** each tab inserted `${svgX(R)}` (static SVG string).
- **After:** each tab inserts `${figBox("name",R)}` = `<div class="absfig" data-fig="name">` + a small control row (`.figctl`) + the same SVG. Elements carry `tabindex="0" class="fi" role aria-label data-tip data-fjump` (added by `fia()` / `fg()` only when `FIG_STATIC` is false).
  - Hover, keyboard focus or a tap shows a tooltip (`#figTip`, role tooltip): the value and its expression with the values substituted.
  - Click or Enter calls the existing `gotoPanel(tab, panel)` (scroll + flash of the worked panel). On touch, the first tap shows the value and a second tap follows the link. Escape closes the tooltip.
  - A crosshair (`data-fx`) follows the pointer on the pressure and stem figures (↑/↓ on the focused figure).
  - The figure selections live in `FIG`, in memory only. They are never saved and are kept across recalculation. A limit state that disappears (Extreme Event I switched off) falls back to the default.
- **Report:** `buildReport()` calls `figStaticIn(clone,R)` on each cloned tab. Each `.absfig` is replaced by its figure drawn with `FIG_STATIC = true` and the default selection, i.e. exactly the SVG string of main. The pile plan is redrawn the same way. `.figctl` and the `data-pile` markers are removed. `@media print` hides `.figctl` and `#figTip`.

### F-ABINT-2. §6.5 lateral pressure on the stem and backwall (`svgWallPressure`)
- **Selector:** "Figures: limit state" (shared). Default = the Tab 6 selection `R.vmSel`, as before. Another state is drawn from `R.buildVM("ls:"+state)`, the V&M integration that already exists.
- **Hover / crosshair:** z, and w(z) read from the V&M arrays by linear interpolation between stations. The tooltip also gives the expression with values, `w = γ_EH·k_ah·γ·(H_s − z) + γ_LS·k_ah·γ·h_eq (+ γ_ES·k_ah·q_ES)` (backwall: depth s and h_eq,bw), with γ from `R.vmGamma(state)`. The expression is shown only when it reproduces the V&M value within 1e-6; otherwise the tooltip says the value is read from §6.1 / §6.2.
- **Click:** stem → §6.1, backwall → §6.2, value labels → Tab 1 §1.3, EE I arrows → §3.6a.

### F-ABINT-3. §3.2a resultant vs kern (`svgResultants`)
- **Selector:** shared limit state. The selected state's row is shaded and every permutation of that state is drawn as a hollow dot with its own tooltip.
- **Hover:** x̄ = (ΣM_v − ΣM_h)/ΣV with the values; e = B/2 − x̄; |e|/e_lim against that state's limit (or "Service I: no limit"); kern inside / outside. The kern, B/3 and e_lim lines carry B/6, B/3 and e_lim with values.
- **Click:** the governing state → §3.2; other states → that state's permutation table (Tab 2 §2.3).
- `best` keeps its combination `c` (display only).

### F-ABINT-4. §5.2b stem M_u and φM_n (`stemCapacityProfile`, new `stemProfAt`, `svgStemCapacity`)
- **Refactor:** `stemCapacityProfile()` loops over `stemProfAt(R,z)`, which has the same expressions in the same order (the only change: the unused `c=R.checks.stemFlex` is gone). It also returns r, t, d, A_s, a, c, ε_t and φ for the tooltip. The profile values are unchanged (report identical; slider at z = 0 equals the §5.2 M_u and φM_n).
- **Selector:** shared limit state. The governing state (default) keeps the §5.2b profile. Another state takes M_u(z) from its §6.1 V&M stem diagram; the figure title says so.
- **Height slider and crosshair:** the readout gives z, M_u, φM_n and M_u/φM_n. The tooltip gives M_u(z) = Σγ·M·rⁿ + H_gird(h_stem − z) + M_ecc with the values, and φM_n(z) = φA_s f_y(d − a/2)/12 with t(z), d and ε_t.
- **Click:** §5.2, or §6.1 for a V&M curve.

### F-ABINT-5. §5.7 reinforcement section (`svgRebarDims`)
- **Hover / focus on A1, B1, C1, D1 and the dowel:** bar, spacing, A_s = A_b·12/s (and A_s,req), cover, d, and ℓ_d = max(ℓ_db·λ_rl·λ_cf·λ_rc, 12) with the values of the section check. The dowel shows ℓ_dh, the available length and the lap.
- **Click:** §5.1 to §5.4 and §5.2a.
- **No selector:** the figure does not depend on the load state.

### F-ABINT-6. §5.6 seat plan (`svgSeatPlan`)
- **Selector:** "Bearing (load case)", governing girder (default) or any girder. For another girder, c_trans, c, A₂ and m are re-derived with the expressions of `computeAll` C-15 `seatM()` (geometry only; the factored load and q_b/q_R stay worked for the governing girder). Selecting the governing girder reproduces the printed plan exactly.
- **Hover:** pad (A₁; and for the governing girder P_u, q_b, q_R, q_b/q_R), A₂ outline (A₂ and m), c_front, c_back, c_trans with their expressions.
- **Click:** §5.6.

### F-ABINT-7. §4.1 pile plan (`drawPilePlan` → new `pilePlanSVG`) and §4.3 pile reactions (`svgPileReactions`)
- **Selector:** the shared limit state, also above the plan. Plan default: the largest compression over the limit states (as before). Selected: that state's governing max-compression case. The §4.3 row figure is drawn the same way (default: the governing case `R.checks.pileComp`).
- **Hover a pile:** number, x and y, the case, and P_i = ΣV/n + M_y·x′/Σx′² + M_x·y′/Σy′² with the values of that case (`perLS[ls].best`: c.V, My, Mx), giving the plotted P. Also D/C = P/(φ_c·R_n) as the plan's colour scale. Inactive piles say so.
- **Hover a row arrow:** piles in the row, max / min / Σ P, the rigid-cap terms and max P/(φ_c·R_n) for that state.
- **Linking:** hovering a pile highlights that pile's "@ pile" cells in the §4.3 table (`data-pile`), its row arrow in the §4.3 figure (`data-prow`) and the pile in the 3D view (`D3.piles`, emissive colour; the last hovered pile stays marked). Hovering a row arrow highlights its piles in the plan.
- **Click:** §4.2.
- The plan draws transparent hit circles on top (interactive only). Static output is unchanged.

### F-ABINT-8. Wing figures (`svgWingElev`, `svgWingPlan`, `svgWingPress`)
- **Elevation / plan:** tooltips on the wing (L, H₀, H_L, t), the governing strip y* (Strength I strip moment), the design section x_s / H_s, the barrier (F, L_t, H_e) and the dimensions. Clicks go to §9.0, §9.2, §9.1 and §9.2a.
- **Pressure — selector "Wing load case":** unfactored (default) or a combination of §9.2. The factors are taken from that combination's own term list `W.LS[lc].tm`; Extreme Event II uses `W.Kee2`.
- **Pressure — hover / crosshair:** EH = γ·k_h·γ·depth, LS = γ·k_h·γ·h_eq, the seismic uniform equivalent ΔK_h·γ·H/2, and CT, each with values. Click → §9.1.

### F-ABINT-9. Integral / semi-integral section (`svgIabSection`)
- **Selector "Load case":** expansion (default) or contraction. The pressure triangle and its label use K_exp or K_con (§10.3), and the movement arrow uses Δ_exp or Δ_con (§10.2).
- **Hover:** p = K·γ·H with the values, Δ_exp and Δ_con, the piles (section, axis, n, spacing, embedment, P per pile of §10.4), and the diaphragm / cap dimensions.
- **Click:** §10.2 to §10.5.

### Governing provision
None: no engineering formula or reference changed. Engineer's guideline CLAUDE.md §6: values quoted in a figure link to their derivation.

## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/abut-pile-handoff — Foundation-load hand-off to Pile Designer: pile layout, per-pile governing loads, integral-abutment data (ABPX) (PR link added after merge)

Cross-tool connection (CLAUDE.md §7 exception): the same PR changes the receiver, `Pile Designer.html` (fixlog/Pile Designer.md ABPX), and HANDOFF.md §4.6.

### ABPX-1. "Send foundation loads": payload revision 2 (additive)   [feature: hand-off (no result change)]
- **Where:** the foundation-loads hand-off script at the end of the file (anchor `/* ---------- foundation loads hand-off (HANDOFF.md §4.6, channel foundationLoads) ----------`), IIFE that defines `window.AbutFoundationHandoff`. New functions in it: `pileReactions(R,c)`, `pileSection()`, `pileLayout(R)`, `pileDesign(R,lsSel)`, `integralBlock(R)`. Changed: `cases()` (anchor `mine.forEach(m=>{ const g=m.tags.join(", "), c=m.a.c;`), `build()` (anchors `signConvention:SIGN, cases:cs,` and `.concat(nErr?["The calculator reported "`), `render()` (anchor `b.p.cases.map(c=>"<tr><td title='"`), the toolbar button's tooltip (anchor `<button id="fdx-send" title=`).
- **What it does:** the payload keeps `schemaVersion: 1` (Spread Footing accepts v1 only) and adds `revision: 2` and, only when they apply:
  - pile branch, conventional / semi-integral abutment: `cases[].pileP` (each active pile's reaction for that case, by the same expression as the pile table, C-8 of `computeAll`), `pileLayout` (every pile in the hand-off axes, x = −x of panel I-7 so + toward the toe; rows, columns, spacings, offsets; centroid, Σx'², Σy'²; vertical, no batter; the panel I-7 section (HP designation and A, d, b_f, t_f, t_w from `HP_SHAPES` through `hpAuto`, or pipe D and t, or square), F_y, driving condition, embedment, clear cover; cap = footing B × footing length × t_f; R_n, φ_c, R_n,up, φ_up, DR, γ_DR; the distribution and head assumption in words), `pileDesign` (per limit state the pile table's largest reaction `R.pile.perLS[ls].best` and smallest `worstMin`, with that permutation's lateral share Hx/n, Hy/n and √(Hx² + Hy²)/n, head pinned, M = 0);
  - abutment type Integral: `integral` from `R.iab` (Tab 10): per pile DL = (DC + DW)/n, DC/n, DW/n, LL of the most loaded pile = `P.Pll/(η·γLL)` (MassDOT: without IM), γ's, η, the abutment's P_g and the MassDOT table P_u; thermal α, ΔT rise / fall, L_exp, Δ_exp, Δ_con and δ = max(Δ_exp, Δ_con) (CTDOT: its Δ_L, `P.ct.dL`); skew, height deck to bottom of cap, abutment length, cap width / depth, diaphragm height, total length, material, grade, curvature, height difference, straight, parallel, rock below the tip, not scour susceptible, MassDOT soil type, U-wingwalls (from the wingwall module, null when it is off), pile section, F_y, orientation, n, spacing, embedment, length; owner and preset (`massdot` / `ctdot` / ""). No `pileLayout` / `pileDesign` for an integral abutment (its piles are in Tab 10, not the panel I-7 group).
  - Notes describe each block; the send dialog lists what else is sent (`#fdx-extra`).
- **Before / after code:** see the diff below.
- **Governing provision:** none changed. The per-pile reaction is the calculator's existing rigid-cap expression (C-8): P_i = ΣV/n + M_y·x'_i/Σx'² + M_x·y'_i/Σy'², M_y = (M_v − M_h) − ΣV·x̄_gc,T (= ΣV·e_x of C-8, e_x + toward the heel), M_x = M_t − ΣV·ȳ_gc. `pileReactions` writes it with (M_v − M_h) − V·x_gcT instead of V·(x̄ − x_gcT); the two are equal (x̄ = (M_v − M_h)/V) and the first is also defined for V ≤ 0.
- **Check case (default project, foundation branch set to piles; 24 HP12X53 in 3 rows × 8 columns, rows 4.25 ft, columns 5.5 ft):**

  - Case "Strength I — V max": P = 3153.435 kip, M_y = +3597.453 kip-ft (toward the toe), M_x = 0. Toe row (x' = 4.25 ft toward the toe): 3153.435/24 + 3597.453 · 4.25/289 = 131.393 + 52.904 = **184.297 kip**; middle row 131.393 kip; heel row 131.393 − 52.904 = **78.489 kip** (payload `pileP` 184.297 / 131.393 / 78.489).
  - `pileDesign`, Strength I compression: pile 1 (toe row, y = −19.25 ft), P = **212.713 kip** = the pile table maximum (`R.pile.perLS["Strength I"].best.Pmax`), Vx/n = 744.2/24 = **31.008 kip**, Vy = 0.
  - Integral, MassDOT, skew 15° (default integral inputs, 6 HP12X84): DL = (717.90 + 72.00)/6 = **131.65 kip**, LL = **52.632 kip**, δ = max(0.162, 0.212) = **0.212 in**, P_g = 259.668 kip, table P_u = 425 kip.
- **Results:** unchanged. `computeAll` (dashboard, permutation tables, `R.pile`, `R.iab`) identical to origin/main for the default project, the pile branch and the integral MassDOT project; the cases sent are identical to origin/main's (the new fields only add); page text and storage identical (`tests/compare.mjs --tool page`).
- **Saved data (§5):** none (the project format is unchanged; the payload only gets optional fields). `schemaVersion` stays 1.
- **How verified:** `node tests/check-syntax.mjs abutment_calculator.html "Pile Designer.html"`: pass. `node tests/compare.mjs --tool page --file abutment_calculator.html`: page text and storage identical to origin/main. End-to-end in jsdom 24 (React 18.2 served for Pile Designer): 45 checks, all pass (fixlog/Pile Designer.md ABPX lists them), including: every pile of all 27 imported cases equal in both tools (max 5.0e-4 kip, payload rounding), and the "pile P max" case of the 5 limit states within 6.3e-6 kip of `R.pile.perLS[ls].best.loads`.
- **Other copies:** none (the hand-off script is this tool's own; `BridgeXfer` unchanged).
- **Open items (engineer):**
  1. The pile-table distribution has no product term Σx'y'. For a layout that is not symmetric about both centroidal axes (inactive piles, staggered coordinates) it differs from the general rigid-cap solution, which Pile Designer uses (with Σx'y'). Not changed here (calculation change); Pile Designer's import warns when its per-pile reactions differ from `pileP` by more than 0.01 kip.
  2. Integral gravity load: the abutment factors DW with γDW and applies η; Pile Designer's integral mode has DL = DC + DW at γDC and no η. ## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/abut-pile-handoff-2 — Pile distribution with Σx'y'; drag load per pile on the hand-off (ABPX2; engineer decisions 2026-10-20 after ABPX) (PR link added after merge)

Cross-tool connection (CLAUDE.md §7 exception): the same PR changes `Pile Designer.html` (fixlog/Pile Designer.md ABPX2) and HANDOFF.md §4.6.

### ABPX2-1. Rigid-cap pile reactions: product of inertia Σx'y' included   [calc change] [MORE accurate; unchanged for a symmetric layout]
- **Where:** new global `pileReaction(V,My,Mx,xi,yi,pi)` after `activePiles()` (anchor `function activePiles(){ return S.piles.coords.filter(c=>c.active); }`); `computeAll` C-8 (anchors `const Sxy=act.reduce(` and `return pileReaction(c.V,My,Mx,xi,yi,R.pile);   // ABPX2: with Σx'y'`), `pileLoadsFor`, `elasticPilePts`, the hand-off `pileReactions`; report Tab 4 §4.1 (Σx'y' line when ≠ 0) and §4.2 (the general expression, substituted for the governing pile, when Σx'y' ≠ 0); the ABINT tooltips.
- **Before:** P_i = ΣV/n + M_y·x'_i/Σx'² + M_x·y'_i/Σy'². This is the rigid-cap solution only when Σx'y' = 0, i.e. when the layout is symmetric about at least one centroidal axis. Omitting piles in coordinate or grid mode can break that.
- **After:** P_i = ΣV/n + [(M_y·Σy'² − M_x·Σx'y')·x'_i + (M_x·Σx'² − M_y·Σx'y')·y'_i] / (Σx'²·Σy'² − (Σx'y')²), with Σx'y' = Σ(x_i − x̄)(y_i − ȳ). x' and M_y are + toward the heel; y' and M_x are + toward +y. When |Σx'y'| ≤ 10⁻⁹·(Σx'² + Σy'²), the old expression is evaluated, so a symmetric layout gives results identical to the bit.
- **Governing basis:** rigid-cap statics: equilibrium of a rigid cap on identical vertical axial springs, solved about the group centroid. This is the method of AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Art. 10.7.1.5 as cited in §4.2; the article gives no closed form. Pile Designer's `computeCapDist` uses the same expression.
- **Check case (default project, pile branch, piles 1, 2 and 9 omitted: 21 of 24 piles):**
  - Group properties: n = 21; x̄ = 0.4048 ft (+ heel); ȳ = 2.4881 ft; Σx'² = 249.4345 ft²; Σy'² = 2751.3095 ft²; Σx'y' = −161.3988 ft²; D = Σx'²Σy'² − (Σx'y')² = 660 222.0 ft⁴.
  - Strength I governing permutation: ΣV = 2977.875 kip, M_y = −7232.475 kip-ft, M_x = −7409.237 kip-ft.
  - Pile 3 (x' = −4.6548 ft, y' = −10.7381 ft): P = 141.8036 + {[(−7232.475)(2751.3095) − (−7409.237)(−161.3988)](−4.6548) + [(−7409.237)(249.4345) − (−7232.475)(−161.3988)](−10.7381)} / 660 222.0 = **339.571 kip**.
  - Results before → after (origin/main → this branch, same layout):
    - Strength I governing pile 3: **305.688 → 339.571 kip**.
    - Pile compression D/C (φc·R_n = 0.70 × 330 = 231 kip): **1.323 → 1.470**.
    - Minimum reaction, pile 24: **−26.756 → −60.411 kip** (more uplift).
    - The toe shear and punching use the same per-pile loads (`pileLoadsFor`), so they change with the distribution.
  - Pile Designer, with the layout adopted: 339.571 kip, every pile equal to within 5.1 × 10⁻⁴ kip (payload rounding).
- **Default project (full 3 × 8 grid, Σx'y' = 0) and spread footings:** unchanged. `computeAll` (dashboard, permutation tables, every pile reaction, every check) is identical to origin/main `f9f3617`.
- **Saved data:** none. `R.pile` gets `Sxy`. The hand-off `pileLayout` gets `Sxy` (hand-off axes, sign reversed with x).

## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/aashto10-abut-r1 — 2026-10-20 follow-up review, part 1: wing Extreme Event II at 1.00, wing resultant outside the base, MassDOT semi-integral seismic, stem shear by limit state, backwall inertia arm and Extreme Event checks, f_y above 60 ksi, AASHTO 10.7.1.2 pile checks, labels (ABR1) (PR link added after merge)

Source: the 2026-10-20 follow-up review (items N-1, N-2, N-3, N-6, P1 items 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, P4 items 32, 33). Every factor and equation below was checked against the AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) text and, for the owner rules, the MassDOT LRFD Bridge Manual Part I (Hundredth Anniversary Ed.). Engineer direction: accurate results, not extra conservatism.

### ABR1-1. Wingwall Extreme Event II: permanent loads at 1.00   [calc change] [LESS conservative; was the strength γp]
- **Where:** `computeWing`.
  - Attached wing: anchor `if(CT){ const gE2=(own==="MassDOT"&&iabType()==="integral")? 1.5 : 1.0; W.gEH2=gE2;`.
  - Independent wing stem: anchor `if(CT){ const gE2=1.0; W.gEH2=gE2;`.
  - Independent wing stability: anchor `if(CT){ const eh2=own==="MassDOT"? 0 : 1.0;`.
  - Texts in `renderTabWing` (§9.1 collision note, §9.5 combination note) and the MassDOT `wing.ct` rule text.
- **Before:**
  - Attached stem: `const gE2=(own==="MassDOT")? +F.gpEHmax : gEHof(Kee2);` (1.50 for active, 1.35 at-rest).
  - Independent stem: `const gE2=own==="MassDOT"? 1.0 : gEHof(Kee2);`.
  - Independent stability: EE II combinations permuted γDC 0.90/1.25, γEV 1.00/1.35 and γEH 0.90/1.50 (MassDOT: γEH 0).
- **After:**
  - Stem (both types): γEH = 1.00 at Extreme Event II.
  - Kept owner rule: MassDOT attached U-wing of an **integral** abutment keeps 1.50 on the active pressure, the basis of MassDOT 3.10.9.
  - Stability: DC = EV = 1.00; EH = 1.00 (AASHTO, RIDOT, CTDOT) or 0 (MassDOT 3.3.2.4); LS 0.50 with the vertical LS on/off.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 3.4.1-1 (γp column = 1.00 for Extreme Event I and II) and C3.4.1; MassDOT Part I 3.3.2.4 (stem EH at γp = 1.0, stability without EH) and 3.10.9 (integral U-wings).
- **Check case 1 (attached U-wing, TL-4, AASHTO, built-in project):**
  - Per-ft junction terms at EE II: M_EH = 6.9295, M_LS = 2.2640, M_CT = 23.4474 kip-ft/ft; M_n = 44.568 kip-ft/ft (φ = 1.0).
  - Before: M_u = 1.50(6.9295) + 0.50(2.2640) + 23.4474 = 34.974 kip-ft/ft; D/C = 0.785.
  - After: M_u = 1.00(6.9295) + 0.50(2.2640) + 23.4474 = **31.509 kip-ft/ft**; D/C = **0.707**.
- **Check case 2 (independent wing, TL-4, AASHTO):**
  - Stem: M_u = 1.50(22.1536) + 0.50(8.6688) + 97.2 = 134.765 → 1.00(22.1536) + 0.50(8.6688) + 97.2 = **123.688 kip-ft/ft**; D/C 2.824 → **2.591**.
  - Stability: sliding 1.324 (EE II, 0.90·DC, 1.50·EH) → **1.216** (now Strength I governs); eccentricity 2.086 → **1.799** (EE II, all permanent at 1.00: e = 6.463 ft, e_lim = B/3 = 3.593 ft).
  - MassDOT, same wing: eccentricity 0.632 → 0.622 (DC and EV at 1.00 instead of the min/max).

### ABR1-2. Independent wing: resultant outside the base   [display / check result] [no D/C value change where the resultant is inside]
- **Where:** `computeWing`, stability `resist` (anchor `const ea=Math.abs(c.e), out=!(c.V>0)||ea>=B/2-1e-9;`), `W.stab.brOut`; the dashboard row `wBrg`; `addD(…, txt)`; `renderDashboard`, the report tables and `abutResultBlock` (show `txt`); `govDC` (skips a non-finite D/C); Tab 9 §9.5.
- **Before:** `q = V/Math.max(1e-9, B − 2e)` (soil) or `2V/(3·max(1e-9, B/2 − e))` (rock). With e ≥ B/2 the dashboard showed D/C = 1,704,756,944.
- **After:** a combination with |e| ≥ B/2 is flagged "resultant outside the base" (overturning) and left out of the bearing D/C. The dashboard row reads **"resultant outside base — FAIL"** (dc = ∞, pass = false); §9.5 works e for that combination; an error is listed. The bearing D/C of the other combinations is still shown for information.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 10.6.3.1 and 11.6.3.3 (e ≤ B/2 is a precondition of a bearing pressure); same handling as the abutment's own bearing check (`brgOut`).
- **Check case (independent TL-4 wing, AASHTO):** EE II: V = 20.368 kip/ft, M_v = 123.663, M_h = 145.541 kip-ft/ft, B = 10.778 ft. e = 5.389 − (123.663 − 145.541)/20.368 = **6.463 ft ≥ B/2 = 5.389 ft** → "resultant outside base — FAIL".

### ABR1-3. MassDOT semi-integral seismic (3.4.6.1, 3.4.6.3)   [calc change: owner defaults and a new check]
- **Where:** `ABUT_OWN_DEF` (MassDOT `seismic.on`, new `seismic.khR`, `seismic.shEQ`); the change handler (owner defaults re-applied on `iab.type` and `fnd.branch` too; anchor `p==="iab.type"||p==="fnd.branch"`); `migrate()` (`S.own.dv` 3 → 4); `computeIAB` semi-integral branch (anchor `if(own==="MassDOT"&&S.seismic.on){ const user=+I.KpE>0`); new input `iab.KpE` (panel I-0a, MassDOT semi-integral); MassDOT rule `iab.seis` (now a shall-check); Tab 10 §10.5; dashboard `iabDEF`, `iabDEV`; `collectInputWarnings` (the share 0 % owner default is not flagged).
- **Before:**
  - MassDOT Extreme Event I default off for every abutment type (3.4.4.3, a conventional SDC A rule).
  - 3.4.6.1 was a note asking the user to set the k_h ratio and the superstructure share by hand; turning EE I on flagged "overrides MassDOT default".
  - The end diaphragm was not checked for the seismic passive pressure.
- **After:**
  - MassDOT defaults: EE I **on** for a semi-integral abutment (3.4.6.1, any SDC), off otherwise (3.4.4.3).
  - k_h ratio 0.5 on a spread footing, **1.0 on piles** (3.4.6.3).
  - Superstructure seismic share **0 %** for semi-integral (3.4.6.1: vertical reactions only, the superstructure force not combined with the soil force), 100 % otherwise.
  - End diaphragm at Extreme Event I: p = 0.70·K_PE·γ·H at its base, the case-2 wall model (M_u = 0.8·p·s_G²/8, V_u = p·s_G/2), φ = 1.0, against M_n and V_n of the §10.5a section.
  - K_PE is entered (new input, 0 = the static Rankine K_p with a warning; for H ≥ 5 ft AASHTO 11.6.5.5 calls for a log-spiral value with the passive-wedge inertia, App. A11).
  - Saved MassDOT projects: inputs still at the earlier default take the new ones, with a one-time notice.
- **Provision:** MassDOT Part I 3.4.4.3, 3.4.4.8, 3.4.6.1, 3.4.6.3; AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 11.6.5.5, 1.3.2.1.
- **Check case (MassDOT, semi-integral, spread, built-in project):** φ = 32°, γ = 0.120 kcf, H = h_bw = 5.0 ft, s_G = 8.0 ft, K_PE not entered → K_p = tan²(61°) = 3.2546.
  - p = 0.70 × 3.2546 × 0.120 × 5.0 = **1.3669 ksf**.
  - M_u = 0.8 × 1.3669 × 8²/8 = **8.748 kip-ft/ft**; V_u = 1.3669 × 8/2 = **5.468 kip/ft**.
  - M_n = 44.82 kip-ft/ft, V_n = 35.04 kip/ft → D/C **0.195** (flexure), **0.156** (shear).
  - Pile variant: k_h = 1.0 × A_s = 0.15 (was 0.5 × 0.15 when EE I was turned on by hand); pile uplift D/C 0.226 (EE I off before) → 0.272 (Extreme Event I).

### ABR1-4. Stem shear and shear friction from each limit state's own V_u   [calc change] [MORE conservative where another limit state governs shear]
- **Where:** `computeAll` C-10 stem loop (anchor `let stemGov=null; const stemRecs=[];` and `stemRecs.push(rec);`); new block after the stem `sectionCheck` (anchor `/* ABR1: stem shear [5.7.3.3] from each limit state's own V_u`); C-14 shear friction (anchor `for(const r of (R.stemRecs||[R.stemDem])){`); `sectionCheck` new option `quiet`; `sectionHTML` (new argument `shearHTML`); Tab 5 §5.2 and §5.5 rendering; the dashboard `stemShear` governing text.
- **Before:** the stem V_u (and the shear-friction V_ui) were those of the limit state with the largest M_u (`if(!stemGov||Mu>stemGov.Mu) stemGov={Mu,Vu,…}`). Shear friction used P_c with the superstructure DC even when the construction stage governed.
- **After:**
  - Every limit state's (V_u, M_u) pair is kept. The shear check runs `sectionCheck` for each pair: β of the general procedure uses that state's concurrent M_u. The largest V_u/φV_n governs; the flexure stays on the largest M_u.
  - Shear friction: each state's V_ui with its own P_c = γDC(W_wall + DC_sup)/L_ab. γDC is the minimum at strength and 1.00 at Extreme Event I. DC_sup = 0 in the construction stage (no superstructure). The largest D/C governs.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 5.7.3.3, 5.7.3.4.2 (β with the concurrent M_u), 5.7.4.3 (Eq. 5.7.4.3-3, P_c as the permanent compression of the same combination).
- **Check case (built-in project, construction surcharge q_c = 0.6 ksf, γ_c = 1.5):**
  - Construction stage: V_u = 1.5 × k_ah γH²/2 + 1.5 × k_ah q_c H = 1.5(0.3073)(0.120)(19²)/2 + 1.5(0.3073)(0.6)(19) = 9.984 + 5.255 = **15.237 kip/ft**, against Strength I 13.248 kip/ft (the largest M_u).
  - Stem shear: before 13.248/49.818 = 0.266; after **15.237/48.842 = 0.312**.
  - Shear friction: A_cv = 648 in²/ft, A_vf f_y = 1.333 × 60 = 80.0 kip/ft, c = 0.24 ksi, μ = 1.0.
    - Before: P_c = 0.90(465.3 + 510)/44 = 19.949 kip/ft; V_ni = 155.52 + 80.0 + 19.95 = 255.47; φV_ni = 229.92; D/C = 13.248/229.92 = 0.0576.
    - After: P_c = 0.90(465.3 + 0)/44 = **9.518 kip/ft**; V_ni = 245.04, φV_ni = 220.53; D/C = **15.237/220.53 = 0.0691**.
  - RIDOT pile project (ADT 8000): shear friction 0.0999 → 0.1039 (another state's V_u governs).

### ABR1-5. Stem Extreme Event I: inertia at the centroid of the stem and backwall   [calc change] [MORE conservative]
- **Where:** stem loop, EE terms (anchor `const zWi=wallApf>0?`); `eqT` gets `aCore`, `aBat`, `aBw`, `zWi`, `WiC`, `WiB`, `WiW`; `stemProfAt` (profile by part); Tab 5 §5.2 (z_W worked).
- **Before:** `Meq+=Wi*(g.hstem/2)` — stem core, front batter and backwall all at h_stem/2.
- **After:** z_W = [A_core·h_stem/2 + A_bat·h_stem/3 + A_bw·(h_stem + h_bw/2)]/A_wall; M = k_h W_wall z_W.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 11.6.5.1 (P_IR = k_h W_w at the wall's centroid; statics).
- **Check case (built-in project, EE I on, A_s = 0.30, k_h = 0.15):**
  - A_core = 4.5 × 14 = 63.0, A_bat = 0, A_bw = 1.5 × 5 = 7.5 ft²/ft → z_W = (63.0 × 7 + 7.5 × 16.5)/70.5 = **8.011 ft** (was 7.000 ft).
  - k_h W_wall = 0.15 × 0.150 × 70.5 = 1.586 kip/ft; ΔM = 1.586 × 1.011 = 1.603 kip-ft/ft.
  - Stem M_u (EE I governs): 137.258 → **138.861 kip-ft/ft**.

### ABR1-6. Backwall: Extreme Event I check, and the MassDOT 3.4.8.1 seismic stop   [new checks]
- **Where:** `computeAll` after the backwall `sectionCheck` (anchor `R.bwEE=null;`); new inputs `seismic.bwStop` (MassDOT owner default on, 3.4.8.1) and `seismic.bwW` (panel I-11); Tab 5 §5.1a (new panel `o-str-bwee`); dashboard rows `bwEEF`, `bwEEV`, `bwStopF`, `bwStopV`.
- **Before:** the backwall was designed at Strength I only.
- **After:**
  - (a) Extreme Event I, any owner, when the M–O increment applies (EE I on, not a single-span bridge per C3.10.9.1). Back face: M_u = 1.00·M_EH + ΔP_AE,bw·(0.6h) + k_h γ_c t_bw h_bw·(h_bw/2) + γEQ(M_LS + M_wheel) + 1.00·M_ES, with ΔP_AE,bw = ½ΔK_h γ h², the abutment's ΔK_h and k_h. φ = 1.0 against M_n, V_n.
  - (b) MassDOT owner, "backwall is the seismic stop" on: F = c·W_sup.
    - c = the 3.10.9 connection-force coefficient (Zone 1: 0.15 / 0.25; single span ≥ A_s; Zones 2–4: A_s, with a warning).
    - W_sup = the input, or 2(DC + DW)·L_tot/L.
    - Spread over L_ab, resultant at h_bw/2 (tool choice: contact over the backwall height). Front face, the panel I-9 bars assumed there; no soil relief. φ = 1.0.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 11.6.5.1, 11.6.5.3, Table 3.4.1-1, 3.10.9, 1.3.2.1; MassDOT Part I 3.4.4.3, 3.4.8.1.
- **Check case (a) (AASHTO, built-in project, EE I on, A_s = 0.20, k_h = 0.10):**
  - ΔK_h = 0.06057 → ΔP_AE,bw = ½(0.06057)(0.120)(5²) = 0.0909 kip/ft at 3.0 ft; k_h W_bw = 0.10 × 0.150 × 1.5 × 5 = 0.1125 kip/ft at 2.5 ft.
  - M_u = 0.7682 + 0.0909 × 3.0 + 0.1125 × 2.5 = **1.322 kip-ft/ft**.
  - M_n = 0.44 × 60 × (15.625 − 0.647/2)/12 = 33.663 kip-ft/ft (f′c 4 ksi) → D/C **0.039**.
- **Check case (b) (MassDOT, built-in project, Zone 1, A_s = 0.15):**
  - c = 0.25; W_sup = 2(510 + 72)(80/80) = 1164 kip; F = 291.0 kip; w = 291/44 = 6.614 kip/ft.
  - M_u = 6.614 × 2.5 = **16.53 kip-ft/ft**. M_n = 0.44 × 60 × (15.625 − 0.518/2)/12 = 33.81 kip-ft/ft (f′c 5 ksi) → D/C **0.489**. V_u/V_n = 6.614/24.80 = **0.267**.

### ABR1-7. f_y above 60 ksi: strain limits, γ3, S&T f_y cap   [calc change] [unchanged at f_y = 60 ksi (A615)]
- **Where:** new globals `abutGamma3()`, `abutStrainLim()` (after `eqEHfixed`); `sectionCheck` (anchors `const SL=abutStrainLim()`, `const G3=abutGamma3(), gam3=G3.g;`, `const fyST=Math.min(+m.fy,75);`); `stemProfAt`; `sectionHTML` displays; new input `mat.rebar` (panel I-2: A615 / A706 / A1035; default A615).
- **Before:** ε_cl = 0.002 and ε_tl = 0.005 for every f_y; γ3 = 0.67; Eq. 5.10.6-1 with the full f_y (up to 100 ksi accepted).
- **After:**
  - ε_cl = f_y/E_s ≤ 0.002 for f_y ≤ 60 ksi, 0.004 at 100 ksi, linear between. ε_tl = 0.005 for f_y ≤ 75 ksi, 0.008 at 100 ksi, linear between.
  - φ = 0.75 + 0.15(ε_t − ε_cl)/(ε_tl − ε_cl).
  - γ3 by specification and grade:
    - A615: Gr 60 0.67, Gr 75 0.75, Gr 80 0.76.
    - A706: Gr 60 0.75, Gr 80 0.80.
    - A1035: Gr 100 0.67.
    - An f_y between grades takes the next higher grade.
  - A_s,ST with f_y ≤ 75 ksi.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 5.6.2.1 and Table C5.6.2.1-1; 5.5.4.2; 5.6.3.3 (γ3); 5.10.6 (Eq. 5.10.6-1, f_y ≤ 75.0 ksi).
- **Check case (built-in project, stem 54 in, S_c = 5832 in³, f_r = 0.48 ksi):**
  - f_y = 75 (A615 Gr 75): M_cr = 0.75 × 1.6 × 0.48 × 5832/12 = **279.94 kip-ft/ft** (was 0.67 → 250.08).
  - f_y = 80, A706: M_cr = 0.80 × … = **298.60 kip-ft/ft**; ε_tl = 0.005 + 0.003 × 5/25 = **0.0056**; A_s,ST (stem, b = 168 in, h = 54 in) = 1.30 × 168 × 54/(2 × 222 × 75) = **0.3542 in²/ft** (was … × 80 = 0.3320).
  - At f_y = 60 ksi every result is unchanged (verified on the built-in project and 25 scenarios).
  - An f_y above 60 ksi that is not a listed grade of the chosen specification is flagged in the warnings (γ3 of the next higher grade used).

### ABR1-8. AASHTO owner: pile spacing, edge distance and embedment (10.7.1.2)   [new check; no computed result changes]
- **Where:** `ABUT_OWN.rules`, three AASHTO rules `pile.sp` (should-warning), `pile.edge`, `pile.emb` (shall); `abutOwnChecks` early return now only for a spread footing; `ownerPanelHTML` AASHTO conventional pile branch.
- **Before:** these checks existed only for MassDOT, RIDOT and CTDOT.
- **After:**
  - Spacing ≥ max(30 in, 2.5D) → warning.
  - Pile side to the cap edge ≥ 9 in.
  - Embedment ≥ 12 in.
  - Listed in Tab 1 §1.0a; a failure is listed in the warnings.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 10.7.1.2.
- **Check case (pile project, first column spacing 2.0 ft, embedment 10 in, D = 12 in):** s_min = 24.0 in < max(30, 30) = 30 in → CHECK; edge 21.0 in ≥ 9 in → PASS; embedment 10 in < 12 in → FAIL.

### ABR1-9. Basis text, file header and labels (N-6, P4)   [text only]
- Basis item 13 no longer lists wingwalls and pile structural design as out of scope. It now lists pile flexure, lateral analysis, the wind sweep, metric units, settlement and bearing pads.
- The file header now names the abutment types, wingwalls, pile structural checks and the owner rules.
- Basis item 3: "floating bridge"; MassDOT 3.1.8.3 is cited for the MassDOT owner only.
- Basis item 4: passive cited to [10.6.3.4, 3.11.5.4], was [3.11.1].
- Restraint-model labels: "Floating — shared (MassDOT 3.1.8.3 model)".
- L_ab → L_ftg in the rock sliding R_n (§3.1), the Service I q (§3.4) and the pile-toe V_up,cr (§5.3) expressions. The code already used L_ftg.
- References: 10.7.1.2, 11.6.5.1, 11.6.5.5, 1.3.2.1 and Table C5.6.2.1-1 added; the MassDOT sections used with the MassDOT owner listed.

### Saved data
- No key renamed and no format change.
- New optional fields, each defaulting to the earlier behaviour:
  - `mat.rebar` (A615);
  - `seismic.bwStop` (false), `seismic.bwW` (0);
  - `iab.KpE` (0).
- `S.own.dv` 3 → 4: a saved MassDOT project gets the new MassDOT defaults on the inputs that still held the earlier default (EE I on for semi-integral, k_h ratio 1.0 on piles, share 0 % for semi-integral, backwall stop on). Values the user changed are kept.
- `meta.defRev` 8: a one-time notice lists the changes that can apply to the saved project:
  - stem shear;
  - EE I inertia arm and the backwall EE I check;
  - wing EE II;
  - f_y;
  - AASHTO pile checks.
- The Input ID changes once (`meta.defRev`); the new inputs at their defaults are left out of it.

- Headless Chromium (tests/lib.mjs; KaTeX 0.16.9, Plotly 2.27.0 and three r128 served from tests/libs, CSS2DRenderer stubbed), origin/main vs this branch, 25 scenarios, every tab and the report rendered:

  - independent and attached wings with TL-4 / TL-5 (AASHTO and MassDOT);
  - f_y 75, 80 (A706), 100; water + ES + slope; construction surcharge.
  - No page or KaTeX errors, and no NaN or undefined text. The self-test passes.

- Each hand-check number above equals the value the tool shows.
- Saved projects written by origin/main (AASHTO default, MassDOT semi-integral on piles, MassDOT EE I, AASHTO pile with f_y 75 and a wing) open with the notices listed above. The MassDOT defaults are applied only to inputs at the earlier default.

### Open items (engineer decisions)
1. MassDOT 3.4.8.1 stop force: c × W_sup with the 3.10.9 coefficient. W_sup = 2(DC + DW)·L_tot/L by default (exact for a symmetric single span). Resultant at h_bw/2, front face with the back-face bars, no soil relief. Confirm, or give the force to use.
2. MassDOT 3.4.6.1: k_h ratio taken from 3.4.6.3 (0.5 spread, 1.0 piles); the earlier note asked for 1.00 on every foundation.
3. MassDOT 3.4.6.1, 70 % of the seismic passive pressure: read as the design pressure on the end diaphragm, p = 0.70·K_PE·γ·H. K_PE defaults to the static Rankine K_p (a lower bound) until a log-spiral value is entered.
4. Semi-integral: the stem EE I inertia still includes the end diaphragm (backwall inputs), which moves with the superstructure (unchanged here).
5. γ3 for an f_y between listed grades takes the next higher grade.

## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/aashto10-abut-r2 — 2026-10-20 follow-up review, part 2: pile combined axial + flexure and shear, unsupported-length buckling, integral-pile geotechnical checks and 10th Ed. interaction, attached-wing loads on the abutment, semi-integral diaphragm inertia, log-spiral K_PE (ABR2) (PR link added after merge)

Source: the 2026-10-20 follow-up review (P1 item 1, N-4, N-5), plus the engineer decisions on ABR1 open items 3 and 4 (2026-10-20):
- compute K_PE by the 10th Ed. method;
- the semi-integral end diaphragm's inertia goes with the superstructure.

R_n and the p-y moment are entered for now; a Pile Designer → abutment return hand-off will be scheduled separately. All factors and equations were checked against the AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) text.

### ABR2-1. Pile combined axial + flexure, H/n shear (conventional and semi-integral pile footings)   [new check]
- **Where:**
  - `computeAll` C-8: new `pileGeom(shp)` and `pileCombined(perLS, ps)` (anchors `function pileGeom(shp){` and `function pileCombined(perLS, ps){`); call `R.checks.pileCF=pileCombined(perLS, R.checks.pileStr);`.
  - Dashboard rows `pileM`, `pileV`; Tab 4 §4.4b (new panel `o-pilecf`).
  - New inputs in panel I-7: `piles.orient`, `headFix`, `MuPy`, `fixSoil`, `Su`, `DfUser`, `Lu`.
- **Before:** axial only (§4.4a). H/n was reported in §4.5 but not checked.
- **After:**
  - **Section:** the pile with the largest reaction in each strength limit state and in Extreme Event I takes P_u (+ γDR·DR at strength) with its own permutation's H_x/n, H_y/n.
  - **Moment:**
    - The p-y pile-head moment, when entered (split on the H directions).
    - Otherwise the equivalent cantilever on ℓ = L_u + D_f: fixed head M = Hℓ/2, pinned head M = Hℓ.
    - D_f is the depth to fixity from C10.7.3.13.4: sand 1.8(E_pI_w/n_h)^0.2 with n_h from Table C10.4.6.3-2; clay 1.4(E_pI_w/E_s)^0.25 with E_s = 0.465S_u; or an entered value.
    - n_h / E_s are reduced by the group spacing factor of C10.7.3.13.4 (25 % at 3D, none at 8D, linear between).
    - Head "auto" = fixed when the embedment is at least 2D (tool rule).
    - With L_u > 0 the moment is magnified by δ_s = 1/(1 − P_u/P_e), φ_K = 1.0 [4.5.3.2.2b].
  - **Resistance:**
    - P_r = φ_cP_n with φ_c = 0.70 (H) / 0.80 (pipe); M_r = 1.00M_n [6.5.4.2]; φ = 1.0 at Extreme Event I.
    - H-pile weak axis: 6.12.2.2.1.
    - H-pile strong axis: M_p for a compact flange; otherwise F_nc·S_x with F_nc from Eq. 6.10.8.2.2-2 (R_b = R_h = 1).
    - Tube: 6.12.2.2.3.
  - **Interaction:** Eqs. 6.9.2.2.1-1/-2 only when every element is compact for flexure; otherwise Eq. 6.9.2.2.1-3.
  - **Shear (φ_v = 1.0):**
    - H-pile: web 0.58F_y(d − 2t_f)t_w; flanges 0.58F_y(2b_ft_f), with k = 1.2 and C = 1 [6.10.9.2, 6.12.1.2.3a].
    - Tube: 0.5F_crA_g with F_cr = min(0.58F_y, 0.78E/(D/t)^1.5).
  - **Square / precast piles:** not checked (note shown).
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.9.2.2.1, 6.5.4.2, 6.5.5, 6.12.2.2.1, 6.10.8.2.2, App. A6, 6.12.2.2.3, 6.10.9.2, 6.12.1.2.3, 10.7.3.13.4, C10.7.3.13.4, Table C10.4.6.3-2, Table C4.6.2.5-1, 4.5.3.2.2b.
- **Check case (built-in project, pile branch, HP12X53, F_y 50, embedment 12 in → pinned head, medium dry sand):**
  - **Depth to fixity:**
    - s/D = 51/12 = 4.25 → group factor 0.25 + 0.75(1.25/5) = 0.4375; n_h = 1.11 × 0.4375 = 0.4856 ksi/ft.
    - I_w = 125.35 in⁴ = 0.006045 ft⁴.
    - D_f = 1.8(29 000 × 0.006045/0.4856)^0.2 = **5.845 ft**.
  - **Demand (Strength I, pile 1):**
    - P_u = 209.38 kip (no DR).
    - H_x = 31.008 kip.
    - M_x = 31.008 × 5.845 × 12 = **2174.9 kip-in**.
  - **Resistance:**
    - λ_f = 13.79 > 9.15, so the flange is noncompact and the weak-axis M_n = 1324.3 kip-in (FLB).
    - P_r = 0.70 × 769.75 = 538.82 kip.
  - **Interaction (Eq. 6.9.2.2.1-3):** 209.38/538.82 + 2174.9/1324.3 = 0.389 + 1.642 = **2.031** → FAIL.
  - **Other head and moment inputs:**
    - Fixed head (M = Hℓ/2): **1.210**.
    - Entered p-y moment of 20 kip-ft: 0.389 + 240/1324.3 = **0.570**.
  - **Shear:** 31.008/(0.58 × 50 × 2 × 12 × 0.435 = 302.76) = **0.102**.

### ABR2-2. Pile axial resistance with an unsupported length   [calc change only when L_u > 0]
- **Where:** `pileStructural` (anchor `// ABR2: unsupported length → flexural buckling about the weak axis`); `beOf` limit λ_r√(F_y/F_cr); §4.4a.
- **Before:** fully embedded only: F_cr = F_y.
- **After:**
  - With L_u > 0 the pile buckles over Kℓ = K(L_u + D_f) about the weak axis.
  - P_e = π²EA_g/(Kℓ/r)²; P_cr = 0.658^(P_o/P_e)P_o, or 0.877P_e when P_o/P_e > 2.25.
  - F_cr = P_cr/A_g; P_n = F_cr·A_eff(F_cr) (H-pile, 6.9.4.2.2a/b) or F_cr·A_eff (tube).
  - With L_u = 0 the results are unchanged.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 10.7.3.13.1, 10.7.3.13.4, 6.9.4.1.1, 6.9.4.1.2, 6.9.4.2.2.
- **Check case (pile project, L_u = 10 ft, pinned head K = 2.1):** ℓ = 15.845 ft. The axial D/C goes 0.46 → **1.77** (Kℓ/r_y ≈ 140).

### ABR2-3. Integral piles: interaction per flange compactness, strong-axis M_n with FLB   [calc change] [MORE conservative for a noncompact flange; HP10X57 / HP12X84 unchanged]
- **Where:** `computeIAB`, anchors `P.cmp=P.lamF<=P.lamPf&&(weak||P.hwtw<=P.lamWc);` and `else{ // ABR2: strong axis`; `iTex` (Eq. -3); Tab 10 §10.4.
- **Before:**
  - Eqs. 6.9.2.2.1-1/-2 for every section.
  - Strong axis: M_n = M_p ("compact, braced: assumed").
- **After:**
  - Eq. 6.9.2.2.1-3 (P_u/P_r + M_u/M_r) when the flange (or, strong axis, the web) is not compact for flexure.
  - Strong axis with a noncompact flange: M_n = F_nc·S_x from Eq. 6.10.8.2.2-2, with F_yr = 0.7F_y and λ_rf = 0.56√(E/F_yr).
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.9.2.2.1 (10th Ed. wording: Eqs. -1/-2 only when all elements are compact for flexure); 6.10.8.2.2; 6.12.2.2.1.
- **Check case 1 (AASHTO integral, HP12X53, weak axis, p-y M_u = 40 kip-ft = 480 kip-in):**
  - P_g = 290.06 kip, P_r = 542.5 kip, M_r = 1324.3 kip-in; λ_f = 13.79 > 9.15.
  - Before (Eq. -2): 0.5347 + (8/9)(0.3624) = 0.857.
  - After (Eq. -3): 0.5347 + 0.3624 = **0.897**.
- **Check case 2 (strong axis, same section):**
  - F_nc = [1 − 0.3(13.793 − 9.152)/(16.12 − 9.152)]·50 = 40.008 ksi; M_n = 40.008 × 65.189 = **2608.1 kip-in** (was M_p = 3615.9).
  - Interaction 0.653 → **0.719**.
- **Unchanged:** HP10X57 (λ_f = 9.05) and HP12X84 (8.98), both ≤ 9.15, so the MassDOT and CTDOT sections give the same results.

### ABR2-4. Integral piles: geotechnical axial, uplift, Extreme Event I (N-4)   [new check]
- **Where:** `computeIAB` (anchor `/* ABR2 (N-4): geotechnical axial resistance of the integral piles`); new inputs `iab.Rn`, `phiC`, `RnUp`, `phiUp` (panel I-0a; R_n = 0 means not checked, with a warning); dashboard `iabGeo`, `iabUp`, `iabGeoEE`; Tab 10 §10.4.
- **Before:** no geotechnical check of the integral piles.
- **After:**
  - Compression: P_u = P_g (CTDOT: + R_T) ≤ φ_cR_n.
  - Uplift: P_min = η_min(γDC,min·DC + γDW,min·DW)/n + min(0, P_LL,far) − R_T, checked against φ_up·R_n,up.
  - Extreme Event I (when on): ((DC + DW) + γEQ·LL share)/n ≤ φ_EE·R_n.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 10.5.5.2.3 (Table 10.5.5.2.3-1), 10.7.3.8, 10.5.5.3.3.
- **Check case (AASHTO integral, HP12X53, R_n = 300 kip, φ_c = 0.70):** 290.06/(0.70 × 300) = **1.381**. P_min = (0.90 × 717.9 + 0.65 × 72)/6 = 115.5 kip → no uplift. Here n = 6 and DC = 510 + γ_c b(h_c + h_d)L_ab = 510 + 0.150 × 3.5 × 9 × 44 = 717.9 kip, as worked in §10.4.

### ABR2-5. Attached wingwalls: loads applied to the abutment (N-5)   [calc change] [default project: less conservative in sliding (U-wing weight); in-line wings more]
- **Where:**
  - `computeWing` with `X.pre` returns the unfactored pair loads before the section design (anchor `if(X.pre){ const n=200, k=Kst.kh*gam;`).
  - `computeAll` C-5: `R.wingAb`; groups `WGv` (DC), `WGh` (EH, in-line), `WGls` (LS, in-line), `WGeq` (EQ).
  - `GRP_OF`; Tab 9 §9.2a; new input `wing.toAb` (default on; not for an integral abutment).
  - `benchState` keeps the self-test benchmark wing-free.
- **Before:** `W.toAbut` was reported only ("not added to the abutment design").
- **After:**
  - Pair of wings, one at each end, symmetric.
  - Weight 2W = 2γ_c t I_1 at x = x_stem,back + J_1/I_1 (U-wing) or x_stem,back − t/2 (in-line).
  - In-line wings: 2F_EH = 2K_hγI_2/2 and 2F_LS = 2K_hγh_eqI_1 toward the toe at their resultant heights.
  - U-wing pressures cancel on the pair.
  - Extreme Event I: k_h·2W at the wing centroid.
  - These loads enter stability, pile reactions and the footing; the per-ft stem strip is unchanged.
- **Provision:** statics; AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 11.6.1.5.2 (wing–abutment connection), 11.6.5.1.
- **Check case 1 (built-in project, U-wings L = 10, H_0 = 19, H_L = 8, t = 1.5 ft):**
  - Wing properties: I_1 = 19(10) − 1.1(10²)/2 = 135 ft²; W = 0.150 × 1.5 × 135 = 30.375 kip; x̄ = J_1/I_1 = 583.33/135 = 4.321 ft → x = 8.0 + 4.321 = 12.321 ft.
  - Sliding, before (construction stage): V = 1152.03 kip, R_R = 0.80 × 1152.03 tan 29° = 510.86 kip, H = 588.90 kip → D/C 1.153.
  - Sliding, after: V = 1152.03 + 0.90 × 60.75 = 1206.71 kip, R_R = 0.80 × 668.89 = 535.11 kip → D/C **1.101**.
  - Eccentricity: 0.707 → **0.642**. Bearing: 0.933 → **0.917**.
- **Check case 2 (in-line wings):** F_EH = 0.30726 × 0.120 × 1923.33/2 = **35.46 kip** per wing at z = 12.06 ft. Sliding 1.153 → **1.299**; bearing 0.933 → **1.085**.

### ABR2-6. Semi-integral, Extreme Event I: end-diaphragm inertia with the superstructure (engineer decision on ABR1 open item 4)   [calc change]
- **Where:** C-3b (`semiI`, `iParts`, `Wdia`), `EQsup` (+ W_dia), stem EE (`aBw=0` for semi-integral), §3.6a worked inertia.
- **Before:** the end diaphragm (backwall inputs) was part of the lower abutment's wall inertia: k_h·W at its centroid (stability) and at h_stem + h_bw/2 (stem).
- **After:** it is excluded from the wall inertia; EQ_sup = A_s(DC + DW + W_dia)·s_EQ.
- **Check case (AASHTO semi-integral, EE I, A_s = 0.30, k_h = 0.15, no wings):**
  - W_dia = 1.5 × 5 × 0.150 × 44 = 49.5 kip.
  - Wall: W_w 722.7 → **673.2 kip**, k_hW_w 108.41 → **100.98 kip**.
  - EQ_sup 174.6 → 0.30(510 + 72 + 49.5)(1.00) = **189.45 kip**.
  - Stem z_W 8.011 → **7.000 ft**; stem M_u 131.64 → **133.58 kip-ft/ft**.
  - With the MassDOT share 0 % the diaphragm adds nothing.

### ABR2-7. MassDOT 3.4.6.1 end diaphragm: K_PE by the log-spiral chart (engineer decision on ABR1 open item 3)   [calc change] [MORE conservative than the Rankine lower bound]
- **Where:** new global `KPE_A114`, `kpeA114(phi,kh)` (after `IAB_RF`); `computeIAB` semi-integral (anchor `const user=+I.KpE>0, khE=`); Tab 10 §10.5; input `iab.KpE` label.
- **Before:** K_PE not entered → the static Rankine K_p (a lower bound).
- **After:**
  - **Method:** K_PE comes from AASHTO Figure A11.4-2 (log spiral, c/γH = 0, wall friction 0.67φ, level backfill) at the active k_h (C11.6.5.5).
    - Below 5 ft: the static passive of Section 3 (11.6.5.5), taken as the same chart at k_h = 0.
    - M–O passive is not used: 11.6.5.5 prohibits it for passive pressure.
  - **Chart values:** read from the rendered 10th Ed. page to about ±0.05 at k_h = 0, 0.1, … for φ = 20, 22.5, … 40°.
  - **Interpolation:** linear in k_h and φ.
  - **Out of range:** clamped and flagged.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 11.6.5.5, C11.6.5.5, A11.4 (Figure A11.4-2); MassDOT 3.4.6.1.
- **Check case 1 (MassDOT semi-integral, φ = 32°, k_h = 0.5 × 0.15 = 0.075, H = 5.0 ft):**
  - Curve values at k_h = 0.075:
    - φ = 30°: 4.87 + (4.57 − 4.87)(0.75) = 4.645.
    - φ = 32.5°: 5.76 + (5.44 − 5.76)(0.75) = 5.520.
  - K_PE = 4.645 + (5.520 − 4.645)(0.8) = **5.345** (was K_p = 3.255).
  - p = 0.70 × 5.345 × 0.120 × 5.0 = **2.245 ksf**; M_u = 0.8 × 2.245 × 8²/8 = **14.37 kip-ft/ft**, V_u = **8.98 kip/ft**.
  - D/C flexure 0.195 → **0.321**; shear 0.156 → **0.316** (V_n 35.04 → 28.41: β falls with the larger M_u).
- **Check case 2 (h_bw = 4.0 ft < 5 ft, φ = 35°):** K_PE = 6.86 (chart at k_h = 0; was 3.690).

### Saved data
- No key renamed and no format change.
- **New optional fields:**
  - Pile footing (`piles.*`): `orient` ("weak"), `headFix` ("auto"), `MuPy` (0), `fixSoil` ("mediumDry"), `Su` (2.0), `DfUser` (10), `Lu` (0).
  - Integral abutment (`iab.*`): `Rn` (0), `phiC` (0.70), `RnUp` (0), `phiUp` (0.60).
  - Wingwalls: `wing.toAb` (true).
- **New-check behaviour:**
  - With these defaults, axial results are unchanged.
  - Pile footings get the new checks; integral R_n starts not checked.
  - Attached wings now load the abutment (unchecking `wing.toAb` restores the earlier results).
- **One-time notice:** `meta.defRev` 9 lists which changes apply to the saved project. The Input ID leaves the new fields at their defaults out.

### How verified
- `node tests/check-syntax.mjs abutment_calculator.html`: pass.
- Headless Chromium (tests/lib.mjs), origin/main (`4964779`) vs this branch, 21 scenarios. Every tab and the report were rendered: no page or KaTeX errors, and no NaN or undefined text. The self-test passes.
  - Scenarios: default; wings off; in-line wing; EE I; pile (pinned, fixed, p-y, L_u with strong axis, pipe in clay, square, EE I); MassDOT pile; integral (MassDOT; AASHTO HP12X53 weak and strong; CTDOT with R_n and EE I; RIDOT); semi-integral (AASHTO EE I; MassDOT, H ≥ 5 ft and < 5 ft); independent wing.
  - With the wings off, the default project equals origin/main.
- Each hand-check number above equals the value the tool shows.
- Saved projects written by origin/main open with the defRev 9 notices.

### Open items (engineer decisions)
1. **Equivalent-cantilever pile moment.** With no p-y moment entered, the equivalent cantilever gives M = Hℓ (pinned) or Hℓ/2 (fixed). On the default pile project this fails the pile at D/C 2.03 (pinned) / 1.21 (fixed). A p-y analysis normally gives much less. Enter the p-y moment until the Pile Designer return hand-off exists.
2. **"Auto" head rule.** Fixed when the embedment is at least 2D: a tool rule. Confirm, or set the head per project.
3. **Conventional H-pile orientation.** Defaults to "weak" (web parallel to the abutment). Confirm the office standard.
4. **K_PE chart values.** Digitized from Figure A11.4-2 (±0.05). Confirm, or enter K_PE.
5. **Attached wings.** Applied as a symmetric pair. A single wing (plan torsion on the footing) is not modelled.
