## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/aashto10-abut-r3 — 2026-10-20 follow-up review, part 3: Matlock–Reese pile moment, skew and transverse loads, 11.6.5.1 nonconcurrency, P_AE distribution and water, semi-integral construction stage and increment, IM on the foundation, integral cap shear at d_v, passive over L_ftg, CTDOT γ_c (ABR3) (PR link added after merge)

Source: the 2026-10-20 follow-up review (P1 item 2; P2 items 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 19; P3 item 30, CTDOT γ_c) and the engineer decisions on the ABR2 open items (2026-10-20):
1. Replace the equivalent cantilever with the elastic solution of a pile in soil whose modulus grows with depth (Matlock–Reese), with a stick-up term; keep the p-y moment as an override.
2. "Auto" head rule: accepted. 3. Weak-axis default: accepted (input kept). 4. K_PE: accepted. 5. Symmetric wings: accepted.

Engineer direction: accurate results, not extra conservatism. Every provision was checked against the AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) text; owner rules against MassDOT Part I (100th Anniversary Ed.) and the CTDOT BRSDM Release 1 (2024).

### ABR3-1. Pile moment by the Matlock–Reese elastic solution (engineer decision 1)   [calc change] [LESS conservative]
- **Where:** new global `pileLatSolve(EI, kz, Lu, fixed, Le, nEl)` (anchor `/* ABR3 (2026-10-20): elastic laterally loaded pile`); `pileGeom` (soil `nhUser`, `DfMode`); `pileCombined` (anchor `const lat=I=>{`, `src="mr"`); Tab 4 §4.4b worked lines; panel I-7 inputs `piles.nhUser`, `piles.DfMode`; migration of `fixSoil "user"` → `DfMode "user"`.
- **Before:** equivalent cantilever on ℓ = L_u + D_f: pinned head M = H·ℓ, fixed head M = H·ℓ/2.
- **After:** with no p-y moment entered, M_max = C_M·H·T per bending axis:
  - Sand: soil modulus E_s = n_h·z, T = (EI/n_h)^(1/5); clay: constant E_s = 0.465·S_u, R = (EI/E_s)^(1/4).
  - n_h: Table C10.4.6.3-2 presets or entered, reduced by the C10.7.3.13.4 group spacing factor (as ABR2).
  - C_M from a Winkler beam solution: Euler–Bernoulli elements to 12T, springs at the nodes below the ground, unit head load, head free (pinned) or rotation-fixed, stick-up L_u with no soil. The δ_s magnification for L_u > 0 is kept.
  - Solver checks (L_u = 0): free head C_M = 0.772 at z = 1.33T, head deflection 2.43HT³/EI; fixed head C_M = 0.927, deflection 0.93HT³/EI — the Matlock–Reese (1960) nondimensional values. Constant k (Hetényi closed form): free 0.3223/β (exact 0.3224/β), fixed 0.4999/β (exact 0.5/β). No copy of Matlock & Reese is in the reference folder; the coefficients were confirmed against the closed-form solution and the published values above.
  - D_f (buckling length only) computed as before or entered (`DfMode`).
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. C10.7.3.13.4, Table C10.4.6.3-2, 6.9.2.2.1, 4.5.3.2.2b; Matlock & Reese (1960).
- **Check case (built-in project, pile branch: HP12X53 weak axis, embedment 12 in → pinned head, medium dry sand):**
  - n_h = 1.11 × 0.4375 = 0.4856 ksi/ft = 69.93 kcf; EI = 29 000 × 125.35/144 = 25 245 kip-ft².
  - T = (25 245/69.93)^(1/5) = **3.247 ft**; C_M = 0.772 (z = 1.33T = 4.3 ft).
  - Strength I, pile 1: H_x = 31.008 kip → M = 0.772 × 31.008 × 3.247 = **77.74 kip-ft = 932.9 kip-in** (before: H·D_f = 31.008 × 5.845 = 181.2 kip-ft = 2174.9 kip-in; D_f = 1.8T).
  - Eq. 6.9.2.2.1-3 with IM kept: 209.38/538.82 + 932.9/1324.3 = 0.389 + 0.704 = **1.093** (before **2.031**).
  - With ABR3-7 (no IM on the piles): P_u = 200.97 kip → 0.373 + 0.704 = **1.077** (the value shown).
  - Fixed head: C_M = 0.927 → **1.219** (before 1.210). Pipe in clay: 1.082 → 0.536. L_u = 10 ft, strong axis: 5.575 → 4.256.

### ABR3-2. Skew: calculated BR / TU / CR·SH resolved on the abutment   [calc change only with a skew and a calculated force]
- **Where:** `computeLongitudinal` (anchor `const skD=+S.geom.skew||0, csk=`); groups `BR`, `TU`, `CRSH` (H_y, M_t); Tab 1 §1.6–§1.8 `skB(...)` worked lines.
- **Before:** the calculated force went 100 % into V_x; groups had H_y = 0.
- **After:** the force acts along the girders: V_x = F·cos θ, V_y = F·sin θ (θ = skew). Groups take H_y = V_y × share at the seat and M_t = H_y·z_seat. Entered V_x reactions are unchanged (they are already in abutment axes).
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.6.4, 3.12.2 (statics of the resolution).
- **Check case (built-in project, skew 30°, BR/TU/CR·SH computed):** BR = 45.90 kip × 50 % = 22.95 kip → H_x = 22.95 cos 30° = **19.875 kip**, H_y = **11.475 kip**, M_t = 11.475 × 17.0 = **195.08 kip-ft**. TU 35.745 kip → 30.956 / 17.872 kip. Eccentricity D/C 0.783 → 0.755, stem flexure 0.435 → 0.422.

### ABR3-3. Sliding with H_y; eccentricity along L_ftg   [calc change] [MORE conservative where H_y or M_t exist]
- **Where:** `computeAll` C-7 sliding (anchor `const dcX = c.Hx/RR`) and eccentricity (anchor `const eL=Math.abs(c.Mt)/c.V, eLimL=`); Tab 3 §3.1, §3.2 worked lines.
- **Before:** D/C = ΣH_x/R_R; e checked along B only.
- **After:**
  - Sliding: D/C = max(ΣH_x/R_R, √((ΣH_x − φ_epP_p)² + H_y²)/(φ_τR_n)). Passive acts normal to the abutment only. H_y = 0 gives the old value.
  - Eccentricity: e_L = |ΣM_t|/ΣV against the same fraction of L_ftg as along B (soil 1/3, rock 0.45, EE I the 11.6.5.1 value); D/C = the larger ratio.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 10.6.3.4, 10.6.3.3, 11.6.3.3, 11.6.5.1.
- **Check case (skew 45°, BR/TU/CR·SH computed, construction fill 10 ft):** Strength I, ΣH_x = 778.93 kip, H_y = 65.11 kip, ΣV = 1712.50 kip, R_n = 1712.50 tan 29° = 949.26 kip. Old ratio 778.93/(0.80 × 949.26 = 759.41) = **1.026**; resultant √(778.93² + 65.11²) = 781.65 kip → 781.65/759.41 = **1.029** (governs). Same case: e_L = 1106.89/1712.50 = 0.646 ft vs 14.67 ft → 0.044 (e along B 0.722 governs).

### ABR3-4. Extreme Event I: transverse case, 100/30   [new load case]
- **Where:** group `EQt` (anchor `groups.EQt=`); `eqSubCases()`; `comboEffects` EQ factor; `permKey`; new input `seismic.shEQt` (default 100 %; MassDOT owner default 0 % for semi-integral, 3.4.6.1); Tab 3 §3.6a.
- **Before:** no transverse seismic force.
- **After:** H_y,EQ = A_s(ΣDC + ΣDW (+ W_dia))·s_EQ,t at the seat + k_hW_wall (+ attached wings) at their centroids (no soil-block inertia, no earth-pressure increment along the abutment, tool choice). Each Extreme Event I permutation runs 1.0·EQ_long + 0.3·EQ_trans and 0.3·EQ_long + 1.0·EQ_trans. Single-span: connection force only (k_h = 0).
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.10.8, 3.10.9.1, 11.6.5.1; MassDOT Part I 3.4.6.1.
- **Check case (built-in project, EE I on, A_s = 0.15, k_h = 0.075):** EQ_sup,t = 0.15 × (510 + 72) × 1.00 = **87.30 kip**; k_hW_w = 0.075 × 722.7 = 54.20 kip; wings 4.56 kip → **H_y = 146.06 kip**, M_t = 1965.1 kip-ft. Case T row: ΣH_x = 450.27, H_y = 146.06 kip; case L: 584.82 / 43.82 (= 0.3 × 146.06) kip.

### ABR3-5. Extreme Event I: P_AE and P_IR not concurrent (11.6.5.1)   [calc change] [LESS conservative]
- **Where:** `eqNC`, `eqFB` (global); R.seis `fB`, `fBk`; `comboEffects` (f_P on `EQd`, f_I on `EQiW`, `EQiS`, `WGeq`); stem (anchor `const cs=S.seismic.nonConc===false?`), backwall EE, attached wing `TEQ`, independent wing stem and stability; input `seismic.nonConc` (default on).
- **Before:** 100 % ΔP_AE + 100 % P_IR.
- **After:** two cases, each checked: A = ΔP_AE + 0.5P_IR; B = [max(0.5P_AE, P_A) − P_A] + P_IR, i.e. f_B·ΔP_AE + P_IR with f_B = max(0, 0.5P_AE − P_A)/ΔP_AE (walls: max(0, ½(ΔK_h + K_A) − K_A)/ΔK_h). The superstructure inertia stays at 100 %. Unchecking the input restores the in-phase sum (C11.6.5.1).
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 11.6.5.1 (Eq. 11.6.5.1-1), C11.6.5.1.
- **Check case (built-in project, EE I on):** P_AE = 10.212, P_A = 8.923 kip/ft → 0.5P_AE = 5.106 < P_A → f_B = **0**. Stem: case A governs: ΔP = ½(0.04440)(0.120)(19.0)² = 0.962 kip/ft at 19/3 = 6.33 ft, inertia 0.5 × 0.793 = 0.397 kip/ft at 8.01 ft. Backwall EE D/C 0.0350 → 0.0293; heel flexure (EE governed) 0.187 → 0.171.

### ABR3-6. Extreme Event I: P_AE distributed as the static pressure; water   [calc change]
- **Where:** R.seis (anchor `const sumG=0.5*gam*d1*d1+gam*d1*hwE+0.5*gamB*hwE*hwE;`); `eqZr()` for the stem, backwall and wings; new input `seismic.hEQmode` ("static" default | "ratio" with `hEQr`).
- **Before:** ΔP_AE at 0.6H (Seed–Whitman); P_AE = ½γH²K_AE(1 − k_v) with the moist γ over the full height.
- **After:**
  - P_AE has the distribution of the static pressure, resultant ≥ H/3: z̄_AE = max(z̄_EH, H/3); the increment ΔP_AE = P_AE − P_A acts at (P_AE z̄_AE − P_A z̄_EH)/ΔP_AE. Walls (stem, backwall, wings): triangular, h/3.
  - With water: P_AE = K_AE(1 − k_v)[½γd₁² + γd₁h_w + ½γ′h_w²], the same layers as the static pressure.
  - "Ratio" mode keeps the old model (increment at hEQr·H).
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 11.6.5.3 (Eq. 11.6.5.3-2), 3.11.3.
- **Check cases:**
  - Dry, built-in project: z̄ = H/3 = 22/3 = **7.33 ft** (before 0.6 × 22 = 13.2 ft); ΔP_AE = 10.212 − 8.923 = 1.289 kip/ft (unchanged).
  - Water h_w = 8 ft: d₁ = 14 ft; bracket = ½(0.120)(14)² + (0.120)(14)(8) + ½(0.0576)(8)² = 11.760 + 13.440 + 1.843 = 27.043; P_AE = 0.35166 × 27.043 = **9.510 kip/ft** (before ½(0.120)(22)²(0.35166) = 10.212); ΔP_AE = 9.510 − 8.309 = 1.201 kip/ft at z̄_EH = 7.68 ft.

### ABR3-7. IM removed from the LL reaction for the foundation (3.6.2.1)   [calc change] [LESS conservative]
- **Where:** global `imSplit()`; `R.im`, `kIM`; group `LL` (`V`, `Mv`, `Mt` × k_IM; `Vim` keeps IM for `stemEcc` and the stem V&M); inputs `fnd.imBuried` (true), `fnd.imFrac` (0 = computed); Tab 1 §1.9. The self-test bench keeps IM (`benchState`, hand-verified values).
- **Before:** footing and pile checks used the entered LL+IM reaction.
- **After:** footing (bearing, sliding, eccentricity, toe, heel) and pile reactions take (1 − f_IM)·P_LL+IM; f_IM = 0.33T/(1.33T + lane) from the simple-span HL-93 support reaction (truck 32 + 32(L − 14)/L + 8(L − 28)/L, tandem 25 + 25(L − 4)/L, lane 0.64L/2), or entered. Stem, seat and backwall keep IM. The integral abutment is unchanged.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.6.2.1, Table 3.6.2.1-1.
- **Check case (built-in project, L = 80 ft):** truck 32 + 26.4 + 5.2 = 63.6 kip; tandem 48.75; lane 25.6 kip; f_IM = 0.33 × 63.6/(1.33 × 63.6 + 25.6) = 20.99/110.19 = **0.1905**. ΣP_LL = 420 → **340.0 kip**. Bearing, Strength I: ΣV 3053.81 → 2913.81 kip (−1.75 × 80.0); e = 1.857 ft, B′ = 9.287 ft, q = 2913.81/(9.287 × 44) = 7.131 ksf; D/C 7.131/(0.45 × 18) = **0.880** (before 0.917).

### ABR3-8. Semi-integral: construction fill to the seat; M–O increment below the seat   [calc change]
- **Where:** `hfC` (anchor `const hfC0=`); R.seis (`semiR`, `PAEab`, `PaAbA`); stem EE (anchor `const sT=shp(Hs,mdS?0:cS)`); basis text items 10 and Tab 10 description.
- **Before:** construction fill to the full soil height; full-height increment ΔP_AE = P_AE − P_A,full at 0.6H on the lower abutment.
- **After:**
  - Construction stage: fill ≤ h_stem (no diaphragm yet to retain soil above the seat).
  - "Static" mode: P_AE on the lower abutment = P_AE × P_a,below/P_a,full at z̄_EH,below; increment = that − P_A,below. Stem: (ΔK_h)γ[H³/6 − (Hc²/2 − c³/3)], (ΔK_h)γ(H² − c²)/2.
  - MassDOT: the lower abutment takes 100 % of P_AE (3.4.6.1: no horizontal restraint from the superstructure): increment = P_AE − P_A,below at (P_AE z̄_AE − P_A,below z̄_EH)/ΔP_AE; stem: (ΔK_h + K_A)γH³/6 − K_Aγ[H³/6 − (Hc²/2 − c³/3)].
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 11.6.5.3; MassDOT Part I 3.4.6.1.
- **Check cases:**
  - AASHTO semi, EE I on: c = 19 − 14 = 5 ft; P_a below/full = 8.462/8.923 = 0.9483; P_AE,ab = 10.212 × 0.9483 = 9.685; ΔP_AE = 9.685 − 8.462 = **1.223 kip/ft at 6.72 ft** (before 1.289 at 13.2 ft). Construction fill 19 → **14 ft**: sliding D/C 1.101 (construction stage) → **0.903** (Strength I).
  - MassDOT semi (Coulomb): ΔP_AE = 9.407 − 7.638 = **1.769 kip/ft at 10.00 ft** (before 9.407 − 8.054 = 1.353 at 13.2 ft).

### ABR3-9. Integral pile cap, case 1: shear at d_v from the pile face   [calc change] [LESS conservative]
- **Where:** `computeIAB` (anchor `Q.c1.V0=Q.c1.Vu;`); Tab 10 §10.5 case 1 lines.
- **Before:** V_u = w_u s/2 at the pile centerline.
- **After:** V_u = w_u(s/2 − a_p/2 − d_v), a_p = pile dimension along the abutment (d weak / b_f strong), d_v of the cap section. When a girder bears between a pile face and d_v from it (girder positions vs pile centers −(n − 1)s/2 + js), the section is at the face: V_u = w_u(s/2 − a_p/2). A note flags the deep region (strut-and-tie, 5.8.2).
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 5.12.8.6.1, 5.7.3.2.
- **Check cases (MassDOT integral, HP12X84 weak, s = 8 ft, h_c = 4 ft, w_u = 39.554 kip/ft):**
  - Default (girders at ±4, ±12, ±20 ft, over the piles): a_p = 1.025 ft, d_v = 40.95 in = 3.4125 ft; x = 4 − 0.5125 − 3.4125 = 0.075 ft; V_u = **2.97 kip** (before 158.2 kip) → D/C **0.014** (before 1.521). AASHTO/CTDOT 1.701 → 0.020 / 0.015; RIDOT 1.952 → 0.017.
  - n = 5 at 9 ft (girders within d_v of a face): V_u = 39.554(4.5 − 0.5125) = **157.7 kip** at the face → D/C **1.513**.

### ABR3-11. CTDOT reinforced-concrete unit weight (owner default)   [owner default]
- **Where:** `ABUT_OWN_DEF` (CTDOT `mat.gc`), owner maps; input handler (γ_c follows f′c while at the owner default); `own.dv` 5 migration.
- **Before:** no CTDOT rule (tool default 0.150 kcf).
- **After:** γ_c = Table 3.5.1-1 value + 0.005 kcf: 0.150 for f′c ≤ 5 ksi; 0.140 + 0.001f′c + 0.005 above.
- **Provision:** CTDOT BRSDM V2 3.5.1; AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. Table 3.5.1-1, C3.5.1. The review's 0.155 kcf is not what V2 3.5.1 gives (0.150 at f′c ≤ 5 ksi).
- **Check case:** f′c = 6 ksi: 0.140 + 0.006 + 0.005 = **0.151 kcf**; f′c = 4 ksi: **0.150** (no change).

### Saved data
- No key renamed and no format change.
- **New optional fields:** `seismic.hEQmode` ("static"; a saved project with `hEQr` = 0.6, the old default, opens as "static", any other saved ratio as "ratio" with the same value), `seismic.nonConc` (true), `seismic.shEQt` (100), `fnd.imBuried` (true), `fnd.imFrac` (0), `piles.nhUser` (1.11), `piles.DfMode` ("calc"; a saved `fixSoil` "user" becomes `DfMode` "user" with soil "mediumDry").
- **Owner defaults:** `own.dv` 5 applies the MassDOT `seismic.shEQt` and CTDOT `mat.gc` defaults to inputs still at the earlier default.
- **One-time notice:** `meta.defRev` 10 lists which changes apply to the saved project.

### How verified
- `node tests/check-syntax.mjs abutment_calculator.html`: pass.
- Headless Chromium (tests/lib.mjs), origin/main vs this branch, 27 scenarios; every tab and the report rendered: no page or KaTeX errors, no NaN or undefined text. The self-test passes.
  - Scenarios: default; wings off; in-line wing; EE I (dry, water, single span, rock); EE I with the old settings ("ratio", nonconcurrency off, transverse share 0, IM kept); skew 30° with BR/TU/CR·SH (spread and pile); passive with L_ftg ≠ L_ab; pile (pinned, fixed, p-y, L_u strong, pipe in clay, EE I); MassDOT pile; integral (MassDOT, AASHTO, CTDOT EE I, RIDOT); semi-integral (AASHTO EE I, MassDOT ×2); independent wing EE I; CTDOT f′c 6.
  - With the old settings the EE I project equals origin/main in every check (refactor of the EE engine verified).
- Each hand-check number above equals the value the tool shows.
- Saved projects written by origin/main (8 setups) open with the defRev 10 notices and the owner-default notices; no page errors.

### Open items (engineer decisions)
1. **Transverse EQ:** wall inertia only (no soil-block inertia along the abutment) and default s_EQ,t = 100 %. Confirm.
2. **MassDOT semi-integral:** the lower abutment takes 100 % of P_AE, including the part above the seat (reading of 3.4.6.1). Confirm.
3. **IM split:** computed for a simple span; enter f_IM for continuous spans. The integral-pile gravity load keeps IM.
4. **Stem with water:** the stem pressures (static and increment) still use the moist γ (unchanged, conservative).
5. **Integral cap:** with girders over the piles the sectional shear is nearly zero; a strut-and-tie check (5.8) is not made.
6. **Passive:** no ineffective (frost / scour) depth is deducted (review item 19, second half); the scour toggle removes passive entirely.
7. **CTDOT γ_c:** the review's 0.155 kcf is not supported by V2 3.5.1; the tool uses Table 3.5.1-1 + 0.005.

diff --git a/abutment_calculator.html b/abutment_calculator.html

--- a/abutment_calculator.html

+/* ABR3 (2026-10-20): elastic laterally loaded pile (Winkler beam on a soil modulus increasing with depth, the Matlock–Reese model), Winkler springs k(z) (kip/ft per ft of pile = modulus E_s(z) = n_h·z or constant), stick-up L_u with no soil,
+   unit head load H = 1 at the top (free head: M = 0; fixed head: rotation 0, translation free). Beam elements (Euler–Bernoulli), springs lumped at
+   the nodes, banded elimination. Returns per unit H: |M|max, its depth z below the ground (negative above), the head deflection. EI kip-ft². */
+function pileLatSolve(EI, kz, Lu, fixed, Le, nEl){
+  nEl=nEl||240; const ns=Lu>0? Math.max(4,Math.ceil(Lu/(Le/nEl))) : 0, ne=nEl, N=ns+ne, n=2*(N+1);
+  const xs=[]; for(let i=0;i<=ns;i++) xs.push(-Lu+ (ns? Lu*i/ns : 0)); for(let i=1;i<=ne;i++) xs.push(Le*i/ne);

## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/aashto10-abut-r4 — accuracy follow-ups to ABR3: integral pile gravity load without IM, stem earth pressure with water, passive depth neglected (ABR4) (PR link added after merge)

Source: engineer decisions on the ABR3 open items (2026-10-20). Items 1 (transverse EQ: wall inertia, s_EQ,t 100 %), 2 (MassDOT semi-integral 100 % of P_AE) and the f_IM input for continuous spans are accepted as built. Provisions checked against the AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. (2024) text and the owner manuals.

### ABR4-1. Integral pile gravity load without IM   [calc change] [AASHTO: LESS conservative; MassDOT: MORE conservative]
- **Where:** `computeIAB` (anchor `P.eqD=own==="MassDOT"; P.imKeep=`); Tab 10 §10.4 gravity lines (`P.eqD` now drives the MassDOT equal distribution, `P.IM` = IM removed); hand-off note.
- **Before:** AASHTO: LL+IM; MassDOT: LL/1.33 (removes 33 % of the lane load as well); CTDOT, RIDOT: LL+IM.
- **After:** AASHTO and MassDOT: LL·(1 − f_IM) with the f_IM of Tab 1 §1.9 (simple span or entered), when panel I-4 has the foundation below ground. CTDOT (V2: dynamic load allowance considered for the abutment and its supporting piles) and RIDOT (BDM 11.3.2: IM in the top 4 ft of the pile) keep IM — owner rules.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.6.2.1; CTDOT BRSDM V2 (integral abutment load rules); RIDOT BDM 11.3.2.
- **Check case (built-in integral project, n = 6, η = 1, γLL = 1.75, m = 1):** f_IM = 0.1905; LL = 420 × (1 − 0.1905) = **340.0 kip**; W_LL = 1.75 × 340.0 = 595.0 kip; P_LL = 595.0/6 = 99.17 kip; P_g = 167.56 + 99.17 = **266.73 kip** (AASHTO before: 290.06). MassDOT before: 420/1.33 = 315.79 → P_g = 259.67 kip; after 266.73 kip; simplified-method D/C **0.4629 → 0.4755**. CTDOT 290.06, RIDOT 314.56: unchanged.

### ABR4-2. Stem earth pressure with water: buoyant unit weight below the water level   [calc change] [LESS conservative]
- **Where:** `computeAll` stem: `pLay`, `lay`, `stEH(Hx, c, hwL)` (anchor `const pLay=(z,d1)=>`); stem loop `hwL` (construction stage dry); stem EE `shp` (layered, as P_AE); stem V&M diagram (`d1v`, `lTop`); Tab 5 §5.2 M_EH / V_EH lines; water warning text.
- **Before:** moist γ over the full stem height (warning: "conservatively use moist unit weight").
- **After:** as the stability pressure (C-3, P1–P3): γ above the water level, γ′ = γ − γ_w below it, balanced groundwater (no net hydrostatic thrust); water height on the stem h_w = min(h_w − t_f, h_soil). Closed form (c = 0): V = k_ah[γd₁²/2 + γd₁h_w + γ′h_w²/2], M = k_ah[γd₁²/2·(h_w + d₁/3) + γd₁h_w²/2 + γ′h_w³/6], d₁ = H − h_w. The construction stage stays dry. The backwall and wingwalls keep the moist γ.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.11.3, 3.11.5; consistent with 11.6.5.3 (P_AE, ABR3-6).
- **Check case (built-in project, h_w = 8 ft above the footing base → 5 ft above the top of footing):** H = 19, d₁ = 14, γ′ = 0.0576 kcf, k_ah = 0.30726. V = 0.30726[11.76 + 8.40 + 0.72] = **6.416 kip/ft** (before 0.30726 × 0.120 × 361/2 = 6.655); M = 0.30726[11.76(5 + 4.667) + 21.0 + 1.20] = 0.30726 × 135.88 = **41.75 kip-ft/ft** (before 42.15). Strength I M_u 112.06 → 111.46; stem flexure D/C 0.3702 → 0.3682, shear 0.2659 → 0.2573.

### ABR4-3. Passive resistance: depth of soil neglected   [calc change only when d_n > 0] [MORE conservative]
- **Where:** C-3 passive (anchor `const De=Math.max(0,(+S.fnd.Df||0)-Math.max(0,+S.fnd.dNeg||0));`); new input `fnd.dNeg` (panel I-4, under passive); Tab 1 passive lines; RIDOT owner default 4 ft; `own.dv` 6 migration.
- **Before:** P_p = ½k_pγD_f²L_ftg.
- **After:** P_p = ½k_pγ(D_f − d_n)²L_ftg: only the embedment below the frost / scour / future-excavation depth is effective. Default d_n = 0; RIDOT 4 ft (BDM 10.4.1 frost depth). CTDOT's 4-ft minimum embedment (V2 10.6.1.2) does not state a frost depth, so no CTDOT default.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 10.6.3.4 (R_ep available over the design life; future removal of soil in front), 11.6.3.5 (only the embedment below the scour / freeze-thaw depth is effective); RIDOT BDM 10.4.1.
- **Check case (passive on, D_f = 5 ft, d_n = 2 ft, k_p = 3.0, γ = 0.120, L_ftg = 44 ft):** D_e = 3 ft; P_p = ½(3.0)(0.120)(3.0)²(44) = **71.28 kip** (before ½(3.0)(0.120)(5.0)²(44) = 198.0); sliding D/C **0.929 → 1.032**. RIDOT (d_n = 4): P_p = ½(3.0)(0.120)(1.0)²(44) = 7.92 kip.

### Saved data
- No key renamed and no format change. New optional field `fnd.dNeg` (0). `own.dv` 6 applies the RIDOT default to a saved RIDOT project still at 0. One-time notice `meta.defRev` 11 for a saved project with water above the footing or an AASHTO / MassDOT integral abutment.

### How verified
- `node tests/check-syntax.mjs abutment_calculator.html`: pass.
- Headless Chromium, origin/main (`6aa5e32`) vs this branch, 12 scenarios (default; water 8 ft Strength and EE I; semi-integral with water; passive with d_n; RIDOT passive; integral AASHTO, MassDOT, CTDOT, RIDOT; pile; MassDOT semi-integral); every tab and the report rendered: no errors, no NaN. Default, pile and dry projects equal origin/main. Self-test passes.
- Each hand-check number above equals the value the tool shows. Saved projects written by origin/main open with the notices above.

### Open items (engineer decisions)
1. CTDOT: should the 4-ft minimum embedment (V2 10.6.1.2) also be the default d_n?
2. Backwall and wingwalls keep the moist γ with water (normally above the water level).

## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/pile-abut-return — Pile results back from Pile Designer: "Pull pile results" (channel pileResults) and a content hash on the foundation-load hand-off (PXR) (PR link added after merge)

Cross-tool connection (CLAUDE.md §7 exception): the same PR changes the sender, `Pile Designer.html` (fixlog/Pile Designer.md PXR), and HANDOFF.md (§4 channel table, §4.6 content hash, new §4.10 `pileResults`).

Before: the abutment sent its pile layout, cases, per-pile governing loads and integral data to Pile Designer (ABPX, ABPX2) and nothing came back; its pile checks used typed inputs: R_n / φ (panel I-7; integral I-0a), the p-y moment (else the Matlock–Reese estimate, ABR3) and the depth to fixity.

### PXR-1. "Send foundation loads": `contentHash` (additive)   [hand-off field; no result change]
- **Where:** the foundation-loads hand-off script (anchor `/* ---------- foundation loads hand-off (HANDOFF.md §4.6, channel foundationLoads) ----------`): end of `build()` (anchor `p.contentHash=contentHash(lsSel? (build(null).p||p) : p);`), new `contentHash(p)` after it, `window.AbutFoundationHandoff.contentHash()`.
- **What:** 8-hex-digit FNV-1a hash of `JSON.stringify({location, reference, cases, pileLayout without resistance, pileDesign, integral})` over every limit state (whatever the dialog ticks). The pile resistances are left out: Pile Designer returns them. Spread Footing / older receivers ignore the field.
- **Check case:** default project, pile branch: the payload equals origin/main's except the new `contentHash` (jsdom: the whole payload compared after deleting the field). The same project gives the same hash in jsdom and in Chromium (`20cd634f`; integral AASHTO `53cdab0b`).

### PXR-2. "Pull pile results" / "Import pile results (JSON)" (receiver of `pileResults`, HANDOFF.md §4.10)   [feature: hand-off]
- **Where:** toolbar buttons `#pxr-pull`, `#pxr-imp`, `#pxr-file` (anchor `<button id="pxr-pull"`); new script at the end of the file (anchor `/* ---------- pile results hand-off, receiver (HANDOFF.md §4.10, channel pileResults; sender: Pile Designer) ----------`), IIFE `window.AbutPileResults` with `check`, `stale`, `match`, `iabPlan`, `defaults`, `plan`, `render`, `open`, `apply`, `clearRes`, `panelHTML`, `paint`; `recalcAll` and `buildReport` wrapped (as the SubLoads receiver does).
- **Dialog (nothing changes until Import):** source, the foundation-load hand-off the results came from, the stale status (PXR-4), each limit state of §4.4b with the matched Pile Designer case (P, H now; P, V Pile Designer ran; M_max, its depth, head deflection and rotation, z_fix), the integral results, Pile Designer's structural resistance (information), warnings (section, bending axis, head condition and free length different from the abutment's; limit states without a case; panel I-7 p-y moment kept for those), and every input that changes (current → new). Options: geotechnical R_n (static, or a field method's required R_n with φ_dyn), per-limit-state moments, depth to fixity, integral moment (nonlinear or linear).
- **Matching:** a §4.4b limit state takes the Pile Designer row with `source.caseId` = `"<limit state>:compression"` (the per-pile governing load ABPX sends), else the non-uplift Group row whose abutment case name starts with the limit state and contains "pile P max".
- **Sets:** `piles.Rn`, `piles.phiC` (static: R_n,stat and φ = φR_n/R_n; field method: R_n = max P/φ_dyn over Pile Designer's compression rows and φ_dyn), `piles.RnUp`, `piles.phiUp` (static, when > 0), `piles.DfMode` = "user", `piles.DfUser` = Pile Designer's buckling depth to fixity, `S.pileRes.byLS` (PXR-3); integral (owner RIDOT / AASHTO, same orientation): `iab.MuPy` = Tier 2 moment about this abutment's bending axis. MassDOT / CTDOT integral: listed only (their methods have no p-y moment input).
- **Governing provision:** none changed; values are Pile Designer's (its Module 01 static resistance with Table 10.5.5.2.3-1 φ, 10.5.5.2.3 field methods, C10.7.3.13.4 depth to fixity; AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed.).
- **Check case (default project, pile branch; Pile Designer with the default soil layer plus SPT N60 = 25, no stick-up, weak axis, free head, per-pile target, "Run all cases"):** R_n 330 → **225.596 kip** (side 67.234 + tip 158.363), φ_c 0.70 → **0.30** (67.679/225.596), R_n,up 100 → **67.234 kip**, φ_up 0.60 → **0.25**, D_f computed 5.845 ft → entered **6.042 ft** (Davisson 1.8T, Pile Designer). §4.4 pile compression D/C 0.870 → 2.969 (200.97/(0.30 × 225.596) = 2.969).

### PXR-3. §4.4b: the Pile Designer moment per limit state   [calc path, only with an import] [replaces the elastic estimate where a case is matched]
- **Where:** `pileCombined` (anchors `const pxr=(S.pileRes&&S.pileRes.byLS` and `const pd=pxr&&pxr[lsName]`), the δ_s line (anchor `const dL=(G.Lu>0&&src!=="pd")`), the row record (`...(pd?{pd}:{})`); `renderTabFound` §4.4b (anchors `const Mtxt=r.src==="pd"?`, `...(G.Lu>0&&r.src!=="pd"?`, `(r.src==="pd"?"Moment from Pile Designer`, ` (PD)`).
- **Before:** M = the panel I-7 p-y moment for every limit state when entered, else M = C_M·H·T (Matlock–Reese); with L_u > 0, M × δ_s = 1/(1 − P_u/P_e).
- **After:** a limit state with a Pile Designer record: M = M_max,PD (the largest |M| of that case's p-y solve, factored), M_x = M·|H_x|/H, M_y = M·|H_y|/H (as the entered p-y moment), **no δ_s** (Pile Designer's p-y solve is a beam-column with the case's axial load, so P-Δ is in M_max; applying δ_s would count it twice). Limit states without a record: unchanged. A record whose P or H/n differs from the governing pile now (0.01 kip + 0.1 %) gives a warning; the moment is still used.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.9.2.2.1 (interaction, unchanged), 4.5.3.2.2b (δ_s, not applied to a second-order moment).
- **Check case (same as PXR-2), Strength I, pile 1:** P_u = 200.97 kip, P_r = 0.70 × 769.75 = 538.82 kip, H_x = 31.008, H_y = 0 kip, M_rx = 1324.3, M_ry = 2608.1 kip-in, Eq. 6.9.2.2.1-3 (flange noncompact).
  - Before (Matlock–Reese): M_ux = 0.772 × 31.008 × 3.247 = 77.74 kip-ft → 200.97/538.82 + 932.9/1324.3 = 0.3730 + 0.7045 = **1.0774**.
  - After: Pile Designer "Abut: Strength I — pile 1 (max compression)", P = 200.969, V = 31.008 kip → M_max = **213.777 kip-ft** at 7.0 ft below grade (y_0 = 5.210 in, θ_0 = −0.0665 rad, z_fix = 14.48 ft) → M_ux = 213.777 × 12 = 2565.3 kip-in → 0.3730 + 2565.3/1324.3 = 0.3730 + 1.9371 = **2.3101** (hand = tool).
  - Other limit states (before → after): Strength III 0.851 → 1.479, Strength V 1.047 → 2.148, construction stage 0.732 → 1.220.
  - Group target instead (Pile Designer adopts the layout, Group row "Strength I — pile P max"): M_max = 213.781 kip-ft → 2.3101.
  - δ_s, L_u = 5 ft (K = 2.1, Kℓ = 22.77 ft, P_e,x = 480.4 kip, P_r = 276.15 kip), M = 213.777 kip-ft: entered as the p-y moment, δ_x = 1/(1 − 200.97/480.4) = 1.7193 → 0.7278 + 2565.3 × 1.7193/1324.3 = **4.0581**; as a Pile Designer moment, δ = 1 → 0.7278 + 2565.3/1324.3 = **2.6648**.
  - The large step from 77.7 to 213.8 kip-ft is the soil model: Pile Designer's nonlinear p-y with its default sand layer (φ = 32°, k = 90 pci) under 31 kip deflects 5.2 in; the elastic estimate uses n_h = 1.11 × 0.4375 ksi/ft. The check case only shows the data path; the soil is the engineer's.
- **Integral (AASHTO owner, default integral project, Pile Designer IAB mode with Tier 2):** M_uy = 24.325 kip-ft linear, **59.557 kip-ft** nonlinear (imported, weak axis), M_ux = 0. Tab 10 interaction before: moment not entered (P_u/P_r = 266.73/861.0 = 0.310 only); after Eq. 6.9.2.2.1-2: 0.3098 + (8/9)(59.557 × 12/2660.0) = 0.3098 + 0.2388 = **0.5486**.

### PXR-4. Marking, record, stale check, report   [feature]
- **Where:** `pxrTagHTML`, `pxrTagRefresh` (anchor `/* PXR (2026-10-20): an input set by "Pull pile results"`), `inpRow` / `selRow` (anchor `ownTagHTML(path)||pxrTagHTML(path)`), `recalcAll` (anchor `ownTagRefresh(); pxrTagRefresh();`), panel I-7 and I-0a (anchor `AbutPileResults.panelHTML(`).
- **Marking:** inputs in `S.pileRes.fields` get the owner-default style (`ownv`, tag "PD · from Pile Designer, <time> (Pull pile results)") while they hold the imported value; editing one clears its marker.
- **Stale check:** "Current" when the result's `basis.contentHash` equals `AbutFoundationHandoff.contentHash()` now; STALE when it differs, or (no hash) when `basis.producedAt` is not the time of the abutment's last send (`bridgeSuite.v1.foundationLoads.by.abutment`); results based on another sender or none: "not from this abutment". Shown in the dialog, in panel I-7 / I-0a (re-checked after every recalculation), as a warning when STALE, and in the report.
- **Check:** deactivating pile 1 changes the hash `20cd634f` → `62a43606` and gives the STALE warning plus a load-mismatch warning for each of the 4 limit states; reactivating it restores the hash and clears both; a surcharge change (+0.25 ksf) also gives STALE.
- **Report:** a source line under the title (`#pxr-rpt-src`) and the §4.4b worked lines.
- **Clear:** "Clear Pile Designer results" (panel I-7 / I-0a) removes `S.pileRes`; the imported input values stay (unmarked); §4.4b returns to the panel I-7 moment / Matlock–Reese.

### Saved data
- New optional field `S.pileRes` (see HANDOFF.md §4.10), saved with the project and in the Input ID. A project without it is computed exactly as before. No key or format changed; `bridgeSuite.v1.pileResults.adopted.abutment` is the standard adoption marker.

### How verified
- `node tests/check-syntax.mjs abutment_calculator.html "Pile Designer.html"`: all scripts pass.
- `node tests/compare.mjs --tool page --file abutment_calculator.html`: storage identical; page text differs only by the two new toolbar buttons ("Pull pile results", "Import pile results (JSON)").
- End-to-end in jsdom (one localStorage for both tools; React served for Pile Designer): 49 checks, all pass: nothing imported → `computeAll` (Input ID, dashboard, permutation tables, all checks, warnings) identical to origin/main for the default, pile-branch, integral AASHTO and integral MassDOT projects, and the foundationLoads payload identical apart from `contentHash`; abutment send → Pile Designer pull (per-pile) + Run all cases → publish → abutment pull: nothing changes before Import, the values above, every §4.4b limit state uses the matched M_max, highlight and clearing, saved with the project; stale cases above; integral path; group target; wrong schema and nothing sent refused.
- Playwright (Chromium, libraries mapped to tests/libs: KaTeX 0.16.11 → 0.16.9, Plotly 2.35.2 → 2.27.0, three r128): the same import gives the same interaction per limit state as jsdom to 1e-12; Tab 4 §4.4b (16 formulas) and Tab 10 typeset without KaTeX errors; report line present; screenshot checked.

### Open items (engineer decisions)
1. Bending axis: Pile Designer's H-pile default bending axis is strong; this abutment's default orientation puts H_x on the weak axis. The foundationLoads import (ABPX) does not set Pile Designer's axis (the `pileLayout.section` block has no orientation), so the p-y moment can be for the other axis; the pull dialog warns. Should the hand-off carry the orientation and Pile Designer's import set `hpAxis`?
2. Integral with Pile Designer's biaxial orientation (skew): this abutment's integral interaction takes one moment, so Pile Designer's other-axis moment is not included (the dialog warns and quotes Pile Designer's biaxial interaction). Keep, or add the second moment term?
3. A stale Pile Designer moment (loads changed since) is still used, with warnings. Alternative: fall back to the elastic estimate until re-pulled.
4. Field method: the imported R_n is Pile Designer's required R_n = max P/φ_dyn over its compression rows (including any of its own rows), so this abutment's compression D/C is ≤ 1 by construction for that case; the static option is offered in the dialog. Confirm the default (field method when Pile Designer has one).

"+f(g.minPen.tipElMin,1):"")+"; controlling tip "+f(g.minPen.controllingTipDepth,1)+" ft"+(num(g.minPen.tipElControlling)?" (El. "+f(g.minPen.tipElControlling,1)+")":"")+". ## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/pile-abut-return-2 — Follow-ups to PXR (#388): H-pile orientation on the hand-off, biaxial integral pile check, stale results not used (PXR2) (PR link added after merge)

Engineer decisions on the PXR open items (2026-10-20): 1 carry the orientation and set it in Pile Designer; 2 the integral interaction takes both axis moments (10th Ed. 6.9.2.2.1); 3 stale results are not used (Matlock–Reese and the values entered before the import), shown for reference only; 4 (field-method R_n default) kept. Cross-tool connection (CLAUDE.md §7 exception): the same PR changes `Pile Designer.html` (fixlog/Pile Designer.md PXR2) and HANDOFF.md §4.6 / §4.10.

### PXR2-1. foundationLoads: `pileLayout.section.orient`   [hand-off field; no result change]
- **Where:** `pileSection()` in the foundation-loads hand-off script (anchor `o.orient=p.orient==="strong"? "strong" : "weak"; }   // PXR2`).
- **Before:** the H-pile section had no orientation. **After:** `orient` = panel I-7 orientation: "weak" (web parallel to the abutment: the longitudinal load bends the weak axis) or "strong". Payload otherwise identical (checked); `contentHash` changes with it (default pile project `20cd634f` → `0562d47e`).
- **Effect in Pile Designer:** fixlog/Pile Designer.md PXR2-1 (bending axis and web direction set on import).

### PXR2-2. Integral piles (owner AASHTO / RIDOT): biaxial interaction   [calc change, only with a moment about the second axis]
- **Where:** `computeIAB`, anchor `/* PXR2 (2026-10-20): biaxial bending (a moment about the other axis entered, iab.MuPy2 > 0)`; new input `iab.MuPy2` (panel I-0a under `iab.MuPy`; `iabDefault`, Input-ID `dropDef`); Tab 10 worked lines (anchors `const iTex2=`, `resL.concat(Y.on&&Y.Mu2>0?`); dashboard detail; input summary row; receiver `iabPlan` / `plan` (anchor `o.lin2=weak? t.Mux : t.Muy`).
- **Before:** P_u/P_r + 8/9·M_u/M_r (Eq. 6.9.2.2.1-2; -1 / -3 as applicable), one moment about the orientation axis; Pile Designer's moment about the other axis was not imported (warning).
- **After:** with M_u2 > 0: P_u/P_r + 8/9(M_u/M_r + M_u2/M_r2) (Eq. -2), P_u/(2P_r) + (…) (Eq. -1), or P_u/P_r + M_u/M_r + M_u2/M_r2 (Eq. -3) when the flange or the web is not compact for flexure (both axes bent: flange b/2t ≤ 0.38√(E/F_y) and web h/t_w ≤ 3.76√(E/F_y)). M_r2 = φ_f M_n about the other axis (φ_f = 1.00): strong axis M_p = F_yZ_x for a compact flange, else F_nc·S_x (Eq. 6.10.8.2.2-2); weak axis 6.12.2.2.1. "Pull pile results" sets `iab.MuPy2` from Pile Designer's other-axis Tier 2 moment of the same solve (nonlinear or linear, the user's choice). M_u2 = 0 (every existing project): unchanged.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 6.9.2.2.1 (Eqs. 6.9.2.2.1-1, -2, -3), 6.12.2.2.1, App. A6, 6.10.8.2.2, 6.5.4.2.
- **Check case (default integral project, owner AASHTO, skew 15°, HP12X84 weak orientation; Pile Designer IAB mode Tier 2 biaxial, nonlinear):** M_u = 57.847 kip-ft (weak), M_u2 = 37.871 kip-ft (strong); P_g = 266.73 kip, P_r = 0.70 × 50 × 24.6 = 861.0 kip → P_u/P_r = 0.3098; M_r = 2660.0 kip-in (weak); λ_f = 8.98 ≤ 9.15 and h/t_w = 16.0 ≤ 90.6 → compact → M_r2 = F_yZ_x = 50 × 120.0 = 6000.0 kip-in, Eq. -2.
  - Before (one moment): 0.3098 + (8/9)(694.2/2660.0) = **0.5418**.
  - After: 0.3098 + (8/9)(694.2/2660.0 + 454.5/6000.0) = 0.3098 + (8/9)(0.2610 + 0.0757) = **0.6091** (hand = tool).

### PXR2-3. Stale Pile Designer results are not used   [calc change, only with an import that is stale] [MORE conservative than PXR where the p-y moment is smaller]
- **Where:** global `PXR_STALE` and `pxrTagState` / `pxrTagHTML` / `pxrTagRefresh` (anchor `/* PXR2 (2026-10-20): PXR_STALE`); `pileCombined` (anchors `pxr=PXR_STALE? null : pxr0`, `pdStale:pxr0[lsName]`); §4.4b (anchors `(PD stale: `, `Pile Designer (STALE, reference only, not used)`); receiver: `computeAll` and `recalcAll` wrappers (anchor `/* PXR2: while stale (hash mismatch, PXR_STALE)`), `apply` (anchor `/* PXR2: the value each input held before the import`), `S.pileRes.prev`.
- **Before (PXR):** a stale import was still used, with warnings.
- **After:** when the hash does not match ("STALE"), §4.4b uses the Matlock–Reese moment (or the panel I-7 p-y moment) for every limit state and shows the Pile Designer moment as "PD stale … not used"; every input still holding its imported value (R_n, φ_c, R_n,up, φ_up, D_f mode / value, integral M_u, M_u2) is computed with the value it held before the import (`S.pileRes.prev`, kept through a re-import); the inputs still show the imported values, tagged "PD · STALE, not used: the check uses the value before the import, …". The per-limit-state load-mismatch warning is not given then (the moment is not used). The flag is set after a recalculation (the hash needs the results and does not depend on these inputs); when it flips, the recalculation runs once more. Current results: used as in PXR.

## 2026-10-20 — PR: claude/abut-approach-slab — Approach slab: panel I-0b, live-load surcharge removal, slab reaction on the abutment, shelf as a bracket, friction on integral / semi-integral abutments, slab design (APS) (PR link added after merge)

Basis: AASHTO LRFD BDS 10th Ed. (2024) for the calculation; owner rules on top (MassDOT Bridge Manual Part I 3.3.1.3, 3.10.4; RIDOT BDM 11.3.2, 17.4.2; CTDOT BRSDM V2 11.14.1CT, CT11.1.1.3, 3.11.6.4, legacy BDM 5.8, 5.11.3). Owner manuals are cited by article only. Every code site is tagged `APS`; search for `APS` to find them all. Engineer's direction: accuracy, not extra conservatism.

**With the approach slab off (the default of every project, and of every saved project except the mapped integral ones below) no computed result changes.** Checked against origin/main (`1a98d61`) for the default, pile, seismic, wingwall, semi-integral, integral (AASHTO / MassDOT / CTDOT / RIDOT), MassDOT / CTDOT / RIDOT conventional and MassDOT semi-integral seismic projects: `computeAll` checks, groups, permutation tables, stem / backwall demands, integral results and dashboard identical (owner card rows differ only by the new approach-slab rules).

### APS-1. Panel I-0b "Approach slab" (inputs, owner defaults)   [input; no result change while off]
- **Where:** `apDefault(on)` (anchor `function apDefault(on){`), `defaultState` (anchor `apSlab:apDefault(false),`), `migrate()` (anchor `if(!S.apSlab||typeof S.apSlab!=="object"){ S.apSlab=apDefault(false);`), `abutMergeState`, Input-ID fingerprint (slab dropped while off), `VALID` (`apSlab.*`), `buildInputs` panel `in-apslab` after I-0a, `ABUT_OWN_DEF` (`apSlab.on`, `apSlab.L`, `apSlab.t`, `apSlab.skew`), input echo (anchor `<h3>Approach slab (panel I-0b)</h3>`).
- **Before:** one input, `iab.qApp` (approach-slab dead load, kip/ft, integral and semi-integral only), applied as DC on the end diaphragm. **After:** `S.apSlab` = {on, L, t, W (0 = L_ab·cos θ), ws, skew (follow / square / ct35), sup (shelf / deck), b_S, h_S, h_E, a_v, far (sleeper / soil), μ, lsRed, qEq, shelf bars, slab design bars}. `iab.qApp` input removed from I-0a (key kept in the state, 0).
- **Owner defaults:** MassDOT and RIDOT: on for integral abutments; CTDOT: on, L = 16 ft, t = 1.25 ft, skew rule "ct35" (follow the skew up to 35°, square above with 15 ft minimum). AASHTO: off.
- **Saved data / migration:** a project saved before this PR has no `apSlab`: it gets `apDefault(false)` (off, results unchanged, notice shown when the owner default is on). An integral project with `iab.qApp > 0` gets the slab on with `qEq = qApp` and `qApp = 0`: its load is applied exactly as before (R_DC = qEq·L_ab on the end diaphragm, no LL, no LS change, no friction); notice shown. Results identical; only the Input ID changes (the value moved key; e.g. integral MassDOT 1.5 kip/ft: `190285B9-BDBB` → `996EB676-792D`). A semi-integral project with `qApp > 0` (not used by main's semi-integral path) gets the slab off.

### APS-2. Live-load surcharge removed with an approach slab   [calc change, only with the slab on] [LESS conservative: the LS of the final state is removed]
- **Where:** `apLsRule()` (anchor `function apLsRule(){`); C-3 LS block (anchor `lsRem`); stem `stemEcc` / `heqS`, `heq_ls`; backwall `heqBW`; owner rules `LSslab` (MassDOT), `ls2` (CTDOT), new `ap.ls` (AASHTO, RIDOT, CTDOT; anchor `id:"ap.ls"`).
- **Before:** h_eq per Table 3.11.6.4-1 (or the owner value) on the stem, backwall and stability in every limit state. **After:** with the slab on: MassDOT (Part I 3.3.1.3) and CTDOT (V2 CT11.1.1.3) h_eq = 0 in the final state, kept for the construction stage (CTDOT h_eq ≥ 2 ft per V2 3.11.6.4); AASHTO and RIDOT: reduction per 3.11.6.5 taken when "LS reduction" is checked (default on), h_eq = 0, construction stage kept. Legacy (`qEq > 0`): no change.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.11.6.5, C3.11.6.5, 3.11.6.4; owner articles as above.
- **Check case (default project, slab on, AASHTO):** before: h_eq = 2.0 ft, LSh = 71.38 kip, LSv = 52.80 kip in the final state; after: 0 / 0 (construction stage LShC = 71.38, LSvC = 52.80 kept). Dashboard D/C off → on: eccentricity 0.642 → 0.429 (now governed by Constr — Str I), bearing 0.880 → 0.835, stem flexure 0.370 → 0.268, toe flexure 0.337 → 0.342. With "LS reduction" unchecked: eccentricity 0.597, bearing 0.903, stem flexure 0.349.

### APS-3. Slab reaction on the abutment: DC, DW, LL+IM   [calc change, only with the slab on] [MORE conservative: new loads]
- **Where:** `hl93End(L)`, `hl93Mom(L)`, `computeAp(R)` (anchors `function hl93End(L){`, `function computeAp(R){`, `R.ap=computeAp(R);`); groups `APdc`, `APdw`, `APll` (anchor `APdc:`), `SUPER_GROUPS`; `comboEffects` (liveOn 3 = girder LL on, slab LL off; anchor `liveOn===3&&k==="APll"`); permutations; `stemEcc` (`Map`, `apL`); backwall (`bwMode "slab"`, anchor `R.checks.bwFront=sectionCheck`); `buildVM` (`MbwAp`); `computeIAB` (`Wapp`, `WapDW`, `apLL`, `apLLn`); §1.4a `apLoadsHTML`.
- **Before:** no slab load (conventional), or `qApp·L_ab` DC (integral); the backwall carried a wheel load (Table 4.6.2.1.3-1 strip, #369). **After:** simple span L_s (far end on the sleeper slab or the subbase); basis: loss of soil support under the slab. R_DC = 0.150·t·L_s/2·W, R_DW = w_s·L_s/2·W; LL per lane = max(truck end reaction with the 32-kip axle over the support, tandem) × (1 + IM) + lane, spread over the 4.6.2.3 strip: one lane E_1 = 10 + 5√(L_1W_1) in, multiple lanes E_M = 84 + 1.44√(L_1W_1) ≤ 12W/N_L (multiple presence included, C3.6.1.1.2, not applied again); per-ft intensity w = max(R_lane/E_1, R_lane/E_M). Total on the abutment for stability / stem / piles = max over 1…N_L lanes of n·m_n·R_lane (N_L from panel I-6b roadway width). Acts at the shelf (x = back face of the stem + a_v) or the deck end (x = back face − t_bw/2), with its eccentricity to the backwall, stem, footing and piles; in all limit states; C11.5.6 permutations add "approach-slab LL off" (liveOn 3). Replaces the #369 backwall wheel load when the slab sits on the shelf.
- **Backwall:** couple about the backwall base M_DC = q_DC·e_bw + w_sh·e_sh, M_DW = q_DW·e_bw, M_LL = w·e_bw. Back face: M_u = max(0, M_u0 − (γ_DCmin M_DC + γ_DWmin M_DW)); front face (new check "Backwall front face", dashboard `apBwF`, `apBwFc`): M_u = γ_DCmax M_DC + γ_DWmax M_DW + γ_LL m M_LL − γ_EHmin M_EH − γ_ESmin M_ES.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 4.6.2.3 (Eqs. 4.6.2.3-1, -2), 3.6.1.2 (HL-93), 3.6.2.1 (IM; no IM for the piles below ground), 3.6.1.1.2, C3.6.1.1.2, 3.4.1 (Tables 3.4.1-1, -2), C11.5.6.
- **Check case (default project, AASHTO, skew 0, L_ab = 44 ft, slab L = 16 ft, t = 1.25 ft, w_s = 0.030 ksf, roadway 3 lanes):** W = 44 ft; R_DC = 0.150 × 1.25 × 8 × 44 = 66.0 kip (q_DC = 1.50 kip/ft), shelf w_sh = 0.15 kip/ft → APdc = 66.0 + 6.6 = 72.6 kip; R_DW = 0.030 × 8 × 44 = 10.56 kip (0.24 kip/ft). Per lane: truck 32 + 32(2/16) = 36.0, tandem 25 + 25(12/16) = 43.75 governs, lane 0.64 × 8 = 5.12 → R_lane,IM = 43.75 × 1.33 + 5.12 = 63.3075 kip (static 48.87). L_1 = 16, W_1 = 30 (one lane) / 44: E_1 = 10 + 5√(16·30) = 119.545 in, E_M = 84 + 1.44√(16·44) = 122.208 in (≤ 12·44/3 = 176) → w = 63.3075/(119.545/12) = 6.3549 kip/ft (one lane governs). Total: 1 lane 1.2 × 63.3075 = 75.969, 2 lanes 2 × 63.3075 = 126.615, 3 lanes 0.85 × 3 × 63.3075 = 161.434 kip → R_LL+IM = 161.434 kip (static, for piles, 124.6185). Backwall (e_bw = 1.25 ft, e_sh = 1.2083 ft): M_DC = 1.50 × 1.25 + 0.15 × 1.2083 = 2.0563, M_DW = 0.30, M_LL = 7.9436 kip-ft/ft; front face M_u = 1.25 × 2.0563 + 1.50 × 0.30 + 1.75 × 7.9436 − (EH, ES at γ min) = 16.23 kip-ft/ft, φM_n = 30.30 → D/C 0.536 (tool = hand). Before: backwall wheel load, D/C 0.303 (back face).

### APS-4. Shelf (paving notch) designed as a bracket   [new check, only with the slab on a shelf]
- **Where:** `R.apShelf` (anchor `R.apShelf=o; }`), `apShelfHTML(R,no)`, `svgApShelf`, §5.7 rebar figure `figBox("apShelf")`, dashboard `apShAs`, `apShAh`, `apShV`, `apShB`, `apShE`.
- **After:** V_u = factored slab reaction per ft + shelf self weight; N_uc = max(0.2V_u, μ·DL friction where the slab slides on the shelf); M_u = V_u,slab·a_v + V_u,shelf·x_sh + N_uc(h − d); A_f from M_u; A_vf = V_u/(φ μ f_y) with c = 0, μ = 1.4 (monolithic); V_n ≤ min(0.2f'_c b d_e, 0.8 b d_e); A_n = N_uc/(φ f_y); A_s ≥ max(A_f + A_n, 2A_vf/3 + A_n, 0.04 f'_c/f_y b d); A_h ≥ max(0.5A_s, 0.5(A_s − A_n)) within 2d_e/3; h_E ≥ h/2; bearing 0.85φ f'_c A_1.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 5.8.4.2.1, 5.8.4.2.2 (Eqs. 5.8.4.2.2-1 to -6), 5.7.4.3, 5.7.4.4, 5.6.5, 5.5.4.2.
- **Check case (default, shelf b_S = 12, h_S = 15, h_E = 9, a_v = 6 in, #5 @ 9 tie, 2 × #4 @ 12 legs, f'_c = 4, f_y = 60):** d = 12.6875 in; V_u = 1.25 × 1.50 + 1.50 × 0.24 + 1.75 × 6.3549 = 13.356 + shelf 0.1875 = 13.5435 kip/ft; N_uc = 2.7087; M_u = 13.356 × 6 + 0.1875 × 5.5 + 2.7087 × 2.3125 = 87.43 kip-in/ft; A_vf = 13.5435/(0.9 × 1.4 × 60) = 0.1791; A_n = 0.0502; A_f = 0.1286; A_s,min = 0.04 × 4/60 × 12 × 12.6875 = 0.406 governs; provided 0.31 × 12/9 = 0.4133 → D/C 0.982; A_h ≥ 0.5 × 0.4133 = 0.2067, provided 0.40 → 0.517; V_n,max = 121.8 kip → 0.124; h_E/h = 9/15 ≥ 0.5 → 0.833 (h/2 / h_E).

### APS-5. Integral / semi-integral: friction and slab weight on the end diaphragm   [calc change, only with the slab on] [MORE conservative]
- **Where:** `computeAp` (`P.F`), `computeIAB` (anchors `Q.Ffr=AP.F; Q.PexpF=Q.PexpT+AP.F;`, `Wapp`, `WapDW`, `apLL`), §10.3, §10.7–10.9, semi-integral seat (per-girder slab share), shear friction P_c.
- **Before:** integral: `qApp·L_ab` DC on the end diaphragm only. **After:** slab DC (incl. shelf), DW and LL+IM on the end diaphragm (piles: static LL, 3.6.2.1); sliding friction F = μ(R_DC + R_DW) added to the expansion thrust (μ default 0.60, Table 3.11.5.3-1, mass concrete on clean gravel / coarse sand; editable).
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.11.5.3 (Table 3.11.5.3-1), 3.6.2.1; MassDOT Part I 3.10.4; RIDOT BDM 11.3.2; CTDOT BDM 5.11.3.
- **Check case (default integral, owner MassDOT, 6 × HP12X84):** F = 0.60 × (66.0 + 10.56) = 45.936 kip; P_exp = 394.605 → 440.541 kip. Pile P_g: before 266.73 kip; after DC 717.9 → 790.5, DW 72 → 82.56, static slab LL 124.62: ΔP_g = (1.25 × 72.6 + 1.50 × 10.56 + 1.75 × 124.6185)/6 = 54.11 → P_g = 320.84 kip (tool = hand).

### APS-6. Approach slab design   [new check, only with the slab on and "slab design" checked]
- **Where:** `R.apDes` (anchor `R.apDes={Ls,h,mo,MlIM`), `apDesHTML(R,no)`, section `o-str-Approach slab`, dashboard `apDF`, `apDMin`, `apDCr`, `apDD`, `apDT`, `apDV` (info).
- **After:** simple span L_s per ft of width; M_LL+IM per 4.6.2.3 strip (skew reduction r = 1.05 − 0.25 tan θ ≤ 1.0 on the LL moment for a slab whose ends follow the skew); flexure, minimum steel, crack control through the existing `sectionCheck`; shear shown (5.12.2.1: a slab designed for moment per 4.6.2.3 is satisfactory for shear); bottom distribution steel 100/√S ≤ 50 % of the main steel; top S&T steel.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 4.6.2.3, 5.6.3, 5.6.3.3, 5.6.7, 5.12.2.1, 9.7.3.2, 5.10.6.
- **Check case (default, L_s = 16 ft, t = 15 in, #8 @ 6 bottom):** tandem M = 153.125 kip-ft (axles at 7 and 11 ft), truck 128.0, lane 0.64 × 16²/8 = 20.48 → M_LL+IM = 153.125 × 1.33 + 20.48 = 224.14 kip-ft/lane; /(119.545/12) = 22.499 kip-ft/ft; M_DC = 0.1875 × 16²/8 = 6.00, M_DW = 0.96; M_u = 1.25 × 6.00 + 1.50 × 0.96 + 1.75 × 22.499 = 48.31 kip-ft/ft; A_s = 1.58 in²/ft, d = 12.5, a = 2.3235, φM_n = 0.9 × 1.58 × 60 × (12.5 − 1.1618)/12 = 80.61 → D/C 0.599; M_cr = 19.30 → min OK (0.239); crack control 0.271; distribution 100/√16 = 25 % → 0.395 in²/ft, #5 @ 9 = 0.4133 → 0.956; S&T 0.510; shear (info) 13.356/15.358 = 0.870.

### APS-7. Extreme Event I: slab inertia   [calc change, only with the slab on and seismic on] [MORE conservative]
- **Where:** `EQap` group (anchor `EQap`), `EQsup` (`apSup`), stem EE (`apIpf`, `zApS`), backwall EE, `Q.apEE` (integral).
- **After:** conventional on the shelf: k_h × (R_DC + R_DW + shelf) at the slab level on the wall; deck support or semi-integral: added to the superstructure share; integral: min(k_h W, F) (the sliding friction caps the force the slab can pass).
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 11.6.5.1, 3.10.
- **Check case (default seismic, slab on):** W_i = 66.0 + 10.56 + 6.6 = 83.16 kip → F_i = k_h × 83.16 at z = 21.375 ft (tool = hand); integral: min(k_h × 76.56, 45.936).

### APS-8. Graphics and report   [display]
- `svgApSlab` (Tab 1 §1.4a) and `svgApShelf` (§5.7) registered as interactive figures (`FIG_FN`, #375); slab and shelf drawn in `drawXsec` and `svgIabSection` with tooltips linking to §1.4a / §10.3; report: panels `o-ap`, `o-ap-shelf`, `o-ap-des`, `o-str-Approach slab`, `o-ap-bars` moved into a section "Approach Slab — Loads on the Abutment, Shelf and Slab Design" with its own results block (`abutResultBlock(R,"ap")`); `ABUT_REFS` line extended.

### Saved data
- New object `S.apSlab` (see APS-1); `iab.qApp` kept as a key (0 after migration). No other key or format changed; no localStorage key added.

### How verified
- `node tests/check-syntax.mjs`: all scripts pass.
- Playwright, origin/main vs this branch, slab off: 13 projects (default, pile, seismic, wing, semi, integral AASHTO / MassDOT / CTDOT / RIDOT, MassDOT / CTDOT / RIDOT conventional, MassDOT semi seismic): `computeAll` identical (owner card rows differ only by the new rules).
- Old saves (main-saved state opened in the branch): integral MassDOT / AASHTO / CTDOT (seismic) with qApp > 0 → slab on with qEq, all results identical, Input ID changes; RIDOT integral, CTDOT conventional, semi-integral with qApp, default → slab off, results identical.
- Slab on: 14 projects (default, seismic, pile, deck support, skew 45°, CTDOT, MassDOT, RIDOT, semi, semi seismic, integral MassDOT / CTDOT / AASHTO, legacy integral): every tab and the report rendered; no console errors, no NaN / undefined; report contains the approach-slab section. Hand checks above match the tool.

### Open items (engineer decisions)
1. The slab LL is taken concurrently with the girder LL (the C11.5.6 permutations also run it off). As the LS it replaces, this is a choice.
2. CTDOT CT11.1.1.3 (written for integral abutments) is applied to every CTDOT abutment type with a slab.
3. μ = 0.60 default (Table 3.11.5.3-1); no owner value found.
4. Semi-integral slab inertia goes with the superstructure share (A_s) rather than k_h.
5. The skew reduction r (4.6.2.3) is applied to the slab's LL moment only, not to the reaction or shear, and not for a squared slab.
6. Backwall and shelf use the per-ft strip intensity; stability, stem and piles use the n-lane total (× m) averaged over L_ab.
7. A_h of the shelf uses the provided A_s: max(0.5A_s, 0.5(A_s − A_n)).
8. Mapped old integral saves keep their results but get a new Input ID.

## 2026-10-21 — PR: claude/abut-3d-integral — 3D view follows the abutment type: integral and semi-integral geometry (AB3D) (PR link added after merge)

Display only (Tab 7, 3D view). **No computed value changes; no input, saved-data key or format changes.** Every code site is tagged `AB3D`.

**Problem (engineer report):** with the abutment type Integral (panel I-0a, #373/#374) the 3D view still drew a conventional cantilever abutment: spread footing / pile cap, stem, backwall, bridge seat and bearing pads, the conventional pile group of panel I-4. Semi-integral drew the conventional backwall too.

### AB3D-1. Integral: `build3DIntegral(R)` (new)
- **Where:** new function `build3DIntegral(R)` before `function build3D(R){` (anchor `function build3DIntegral(R){`), called at the top of `build3D` (anchor `if(iabType()==="integral"&&R.iab&&R.iab.integ&&R.iab.pile){ build3DIntegral(R); return; }`).
- **After:** the inputs of the Tab 10 section figure (`svgIabSection`, §10.0): one wall b × (h_c + h_d) over L_ab (panel I-0a), drawn as the pile cap (0 … h_c) and the end diaphragm (h_c … H) with the seat-level edge between them; see-through, so the girder ends and the pile embedment show. Girder stubs (I-shape, depth `iab.dg`, capped at h_d − deck + h_c/2) cast into the diaphragm, crossing the cap centreline at the girder positions of panel I-5; deck over them. No seat, no bearing pads. One row of H-piles (`iab.sec`, actual d, b_f, t_f, t_w of the section) on the cap centreline at `R.iab.pile.xs` (spacing `iab.sp` along the abutment), web parallel to the abutment CL for "weak" and normal to it for "strong"; each pile runs from `iab.embed` above the cap bottom down to min(L_pile, max(8, 1.5H)) (label says "cut" when shorter than L_pile). Approach slab (panel I-0b, `R.ap`) and its shelf when on; wings (panel I-13) attached to the back face of the integral wall; backfill behind the wall and the front fill over `iab.Dfront` (soil toggle). Girder reaction arrows (same `perBearingLoads`) at each girder on the cap centreline at the seat level; earth-pressure arrows on the back face over H with the shape K_exp·γ·z (K_exp of §10.3; label "EH: K = …"); the conventional surcharge band and water plane are not drawn for integral. Dimensions: b, L_ab, H = h_d + h_c, seat level, pile section / axis / n @ s, embedment, skew.
- **Pile highlight (#375):** the integral piles are registered in `D3.piles` as pile 1 … n, so `d3PileHL()` lights them like the conventional ones.

### AB3D-2. Semi-integral: lower abutment + end diaphragm on the bearings
- **Where:** `build3D` (anchor `const semi=iabType()==="semi";`), wall shape (anchor `if(semi){ wsh.moveTo(...pt(g.Ltoe,tf)); wsh.lineTo(...pt(xStemTopFront,tf+hstem)); wsh.lineTo(...pt(xStemBack,tf+hstem));`), new `d3SemiParts(R,T,o)` (anchor `function d3SemiParts(R,T,o){`), called after the wings (anchor `if(semi) d3SemiParts(`).
- **After:** the lower abutment (footing and piles of panel I-4, stem up to the seat at t_f + h_stem: no backwall); the end diaphragm t_bw × h_bw over L_ab (panel I-1) behind the girders, its bottom at the girder bottoms (on the 0.5-ft schematic bearing pads, as in Tab 10's figure: the joint above the seat), moving with the superstructure; girder stubs on the bearing pads (the pads, arrows, earth pressure, surcharge, water, dimensions as before), girder i crossing the bearing line at its position; deck; approach slab and shelf when on; wings as configured.

### AB3D-3. Shared helpers (new)
- `d3Add`, `d3PlanGeo` (plan polygon extruded vertically), `d3SecGeo` (section extruded along the abutment), `d3Mats`, `d3Super` (girder stubs and deck at the skew θ of panel I-1: girder direction (−cos θ, sin θ) in plan; the deck a parallelogram), `d3ApSlab` (approach slab of `R.ap`: near edge along the back face, length W/cos θ; ends follow the skew, or the far end square when `R.ap.rule` is "square", the shorter side L; shelf b_S, h_S, h_E below it).
- **Skew:** the girders, the deck and the approach slab run at θ to the normal of the abutment; the piles stay square to the abutment (their orientation is defined relative to the abutment CL, spaced along it). The plan sense of the skew is schematic (the inputs give its magnitude only).

### AB3D-4. Wing block moved to `d3Wings` (no change)
- **Where:** new `function d3Wings(R,T,cmat,edgeMat,xb,yTop,Lab){` before `build3D`; the block in `build3D` (anchor before: `// WING: wingwalls (panel I-13), schematic: elevation of each wing extruded by its thickness`) replaced by `d3Wings(R,T,cmat,edgeMat,xStemBack-cx,tf+hstem+hbw,Lab);`. The body is the same code with `xStemBack-cx` → `xb` and `yTop=tf+hstem+hbw` → the `yTop` argument, so the integral view attaches the wings to its wall.

**Conventional: unchanged.** Same objects in the same order.

**Governing provision:** none (display). Calculation references unchanged.

**Check case / how verified (headless Chromium, three r128 from tests/libs, CSS2DRenderer stubbed, origin/main `24e1cf8` vs branch):**
- Scene graph of `D3.group` (every object: type, geometry vertex positions, position, rotation, scale, material type, colour, opacity): **identical** for conventional default (180 objects), conventional on piles with wings and skew 20° (204), conventional with independent wings (184).
- `computeAll()` (JSON, functions dropped): identical main vs branch in all 7 cases (conventional ×3, integral MassDOT skew 20° weak axis with U-wings and approach slab, integral CTDOT skew 30° strong axis with U-wings and a square-ended approach slab, semi-integral RIDOT skew 20° on piles with wings and slab, semi-integral AASHTO skew 0 with slab on a shelf).
- No console errors (the KaTeX 0.16.11 and Plotly 2.35.2 CDN requests are not in tests/libs and are blocked on both sides).
- Screenshots looked at: integral: the girders frame into the wall above the seat level, no bearings, piles under the cap and inside it over the embedment, flanges across the cap for weak axis and along it for strong axis, the deck, girders and slab skewed; semi-integral: bearings under the girders on the stem top, the diaphragm above them with the gap to the seat, no backwall. Display only. Basis of the audit: the read-only output-tab audit of 2026-10-21 (integral and semi-integral abutments). Every code site is tagged `ABT`; search for `ABT` to find them all. **No computed value changes:** `computeAll()` (every key of `R` except `R.dash` and `R.own`) and the Input ID are identical to origin/main (`4468f47`) for all three types under all four owners (see "How verified"). `R.dash` gains rows only (ABT-2); `R.own` lists fewer owner-default rows for an integral abutment (ABT-3).

### ABT-1. Check counts and "DESIGN INCOMPLETE"   [display]
- **Where:** new `DASH_INFO`, `dashStatus(R)` (anchor `function dashStatus(R){`), `renderDashboard` (anchor `const nf=R.nFail, DS=dashStatus(R);`), `buildReport` (§1 text, anchor `"All "+DS.nChk+" code checks PASS"`; cover banner, anchor `rpt-banner ${R.nFail===0?(DS.inc?'inc':'ok'):'bad'}`), CSS `#report .rpt-banner.inc`.
- **Before:** dashboard `ALL ${R.dash.length} CHECKS PASS` and report §1 `All ${R.dash.length} code checks PASS` counted the n/a rows; the report cover counted `R.dash.filter(d=>d.pass!==null).length`. Example: integral, AASHTO owner, default project: dashboard "ALL 17 CHECKS PASS", cover "15 coded checks", with the integral pile interaction and the geotechnical check both n/a (not entered).
- **After:** `dashStatus(R)` = {nChk = rows with PASS/FAIL, nNA = n/a rows, why = the required n/a rows (every n/a row except `apDV`, the approach-slab shear information row) plus, for a semi-integral abutment, "bearing shear from the superstructure movement" when the TU calculation is off (panel I-6b) and no TU reaction is entered (panel I-5)}. Dashboard: `ALL nChk CHECKS PASS` when complete; amber chip "DESIGN INCOMPLETE — inputs needed" + "nChk checked, all pass" when `why` is not empty (also shown beside the red FAIL chip); "· nNA not checked (n/a)"; a note listing each missing check with a link to its panel. Report: §1 "All nChk code checks PASS (k rows n/a, not checked)." plus the incomplete list with "see §" links; banner amber "DESIGN INCOMPLETE — k NOT CHECKED" (or "n CHECK(S) FAIL · DESIGN INCOMPLETE"), detail "nChk coded checks (k n/a)". Dashboard and report now use the same count.
- **Check case (integral, AASHTO, default project):** before: dashboard "ALL 17 CHECKS PASS", cover "15 coded checks". After (17 + 3 crack rows = 20 rows): "DESIGN INCOMPLETE — inputs needed · 18 checked, all pass · 2 not checked (n/a)"; cover "18 coded checks (2 n/a)"; list: integral pile axial + flexure (pile-head moment not entered), geotechnical axial (R_n not entered). With R_n = 400 kip and M_u,py = 60 kip-ft entered: "ALL 20 CHECKS PASS".
- **Note:** the conventional default project has the stem dowel lap splice not detailed (`reinf.dwlLap = 0`, an n/a row), so it now shows "DESIGN INCOMPLETE" too; that row was already n/a before.

The MassDOT `iab.misc` note read "not modelled" although the approach slab is modelled since APS.

The owner defaults are still applied exactly as before (only the listing changes). `iab.misc` value: "approach slab modelled (panel I-0b, §1.4a; rule 3.10.4 below)" (or "approach slab off …") "; superstructure types and the crushed-stone trench not modelled — detail per Part II Ch. 15".

### Open items (engineer decisions)
1. Conventional default projects now show "DESIGN INCOMPLETE" because the stem dowel lap splice is not detailed (n/a). Treated as a required check; say if it should count as information only.
2. Wingwalls of an integral abutment: `computeWing` picks the earth-pressure state and k_h factor from `fnd.branch` (spread by default), not from the integral piles; MassDOT 3.1.6 / 3.4.6.3 would give K0 and the full A_s on piles. Calculation item, not changed here.
3. The semi-integral note "bearing shear from movement not computed" is raised by computeIAB whenever TU is off, even with TU reactions entered; the incomplete flag uses "TU off and no TU reaction entered". To be settled with PR 2 (c).

## 2026-10-21 — PR: claude/abut-tabs-1b — Integral abutment content in Tabs 1–6 and 8, Tab 3 hidden, semi-integral end diaphragm in Tabs 1, 5, 6, 8, integral wing height, dowel lap as information (ABT2, part 1b) (PR link added after merge)

Every code site is tagged `ABT2`; search for `ABT2` to find them all. Basis: AASHTO LRFD BDS 10th Ed. (2024); owner methods as in Tab 10. Engineer's decisions of 2026-10-21: the stem dowel lap with no lap entered is information only; integral U-wing height limited to the integral wall height.

**Computed results.** Conventional: `computeAll()` identical to origin/main (`af43d24`) and every tab's text and SVG identical (Plotly element ids normalized). Semi-integral: `computeAll()` identical. Integral without wingwalls: identical. Integral with an attached wing taller than h_c + h_d: the wing results change (ABT2-6, §4 callout).

- **Where:** `computeWing` (anchor `const H0in=Math.max(0.5,+w.H0||0), HwI=`), Tab 9 §9.0 note (anchor `<b>Integral abutment:</b> the wing hangs from the integral wall`), select change handler (anchor `if(p==="iab.type"&&raw==="integral"&&S.wing`).

The 3D view and the wing design use the limited H_0. Other types and independent wings: unchanged.

- **Check case (integral AASHTO default, U-wing L = 10 ft, H_L = 8 ft, bottom tapered, K = 0.3073, γ = 0.120 kcf, junction method "total moment / H_0"):** before H_0 = 19 ft: ∫h² dx = (19³ − 8³)/(3 × 1.1) = 1923.33, ∫h²x dx = 361(50) − 41.8(1000/3) + 1.21(2500) = 7141.7 → M_EH = ½Kγ × 7141.7 = 0.018435 × 7141.7 = 131.66 kip-ft, M_LS = 43.02; per ft: 131.66/19 = 6.929, 43.02/19 = 2.264 → M_u = 1.50(6.929) + 1.75(2.264) = 14.356 kip-ft/ft; φM_n = 40.11 → D/C 0.358. After H_0 = 9 ft: h = 9 − 0.1x, ∫h² dx = (9³ − 8³)/0.3 = 723.33, ∫h²x dx = 81(50) − 1.8(1000/3) + 0.01(2500) = 3475 → M_EH = 0.018435 × 3475 = 64.06 kip-ft, M_LS = 30.73; per ft 7.118 and 3.414 → M_u = 1.50(7.118) + 1.75(3.414) = 16.652 kip-ft/ft → D/C 0.415 (tool 0.415).

Junction bar development and S&T unchanged. More conservative per ft (a shorter junction), less total force.

## 2026-10-21 — PR: claude/abut-calc-gaps — Integral / semi-integral calculation gaps: wing weight on the integral piles, semi-integral end-diaphragm dead load, bearing shear from movement on by default, integral Extreme Event I, integral wing earth pressure and k_h (ABC) (PR link added after merge)

Basis: AASHTO LRFD BDS 10th Ed. (2024); owner rules as in Tab 10. Engineer's decisions of 2026-10-21 (accuracy, not extra conservatism). Every code site is tagged `ABC`; search for `ABC` to find them all. **Conventional abutments: no result changes** (`computeAll` identical to origin/main `eac35f4`, with and without seismic, spread and piles).

### ABC (a). Integral: attached wing weight on the integral piles   [calc change] [MORE conservative]
- **Where:** `computeIAB` (anchor `Q.Wwing=0; Q.wingW1=0;`), `P.Pdl=eta*(gDC*(Q.DC+Q.Wwing)+gDW*Q.DW)/n;`, `Pdlmin`, `geo.ee.Pee`; §10.4 display (`W_{wing} = 2\,\gamma_c\,t\,I_1`), Tab 1 §1.9 ledger, Tab 8 §8.1, Tab 9 §9.2a note.
- **Before:** `P.Pdl=eta*(gDC*Q.DC+gDW*Q.DW)/n` — the attached U-wings of an integral abutment were on no load path (`R.wingAb` is skipped for integral). **After:** `P.Pdl=eta*(gDC*(Q.DC+Q.Wwing)+gDW*Q.DW)/n`, W_wing = 2·γc·t·I1 of the attached pair (the same weight as the conventional path), also in the uplift minimum and the Extreme Event I pile load; rigid cap, symmetric pair → equal share per pile. Not on cap case 1 (the wings hang at the cap ends, outside the interior spans). "Apply to the abutment" (panel I-13) honoured.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.5.1, Tables 3.4.1-1/-2; owner pile method of Tab 10 §10.4 unchanged.

Smallest pile load (uplift) +5.738 kip (0.90 × 38.25/6).

### ABC (b). Semi-integral: end-diaphragm dead load — counted once, on the bearings   [calc change]
- **Check of the double count:** the tool counted the end diaphragm once (t_bw·h_bw·γc·L_ab as abutment concrete "Backwall" in DCsub; its seismic mass moved to the superstructure share, ABR2). It is not in the girder DC reactions unless the user put it there; the superstructure tools of the suite do not include the concrete end diaphragm. So there was no double count inside the tool, but (1) the load acted at the backwall centroid instead of the bearing line, (2) it was present in the construction stage although it is cast with the deck, (3) it was missing from the bearing reactions, and (4) a user whose girder reactions already include it got it twice.
- **Where:** C-2 self-weights (anchor `const semiDia=iabType()==="semi", Wdia0=`), `groups.DCsup` (anchor `V:agg.DC.P+WdiaAdd`), seismic (`iParts=parts, Wdia=semiI? WdiaAdd : 0`), connection force (`Wperm=agg.DC.P+WdiaAdd+agg.DW.P`), shear friction (`ns*groups.DCsup.V`), bearing on concrete (`if(WdiaAdd>0){ const d=GP.DC[1]*WdiaAdd/`), Tab 1 §1.2 note, new input `iab.diaRx` (panel I-0a checkbox "End-diaphragm weight already included in the girder DC reactions", default off).
- **Before:** `parts.push({name:"Backwall", …, x:xBwFront+g.tbw/2})` for every type. **After (semi-integral):** no "Backwall" part; `DCsup.V = ΣP_DC + W_dia` at x_brg (not in the construction stage); bearing reaction per girder + γ_DC·W_dia/N; nothing added when `iab.diaRx` is checked.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.5.1, 3.4.1 (construction stage: Design basis §10), 5.6.5 (bearing).
- **Check (semi-integral AASHTO default, TU on in both):** W_dia = 1.50 × 5.00 × 0.150 × 44.0 = 49.5 kip; x moves 7.25 → 5.25 ft from the toe: DCsub V 722.70 → 673.20, M_v 4422.83 → 4063.95 (−49.5 × 7.25); DCsup V 510.0 → 559.5, M_v 2677.5 → 2937.38 (+49.5 × 5.25). Bearing (girder 1, Strength I): P_u = 246.75 + 1.25 × 49.5/6 = 257.06 kip → q_b = 257.06/432 = 0.595 ksi, D/C 0.120 → 0.125. Eccentricity e 2.407 → 2.459 ft. Dashboard (AASHTO, TU on → + this change): ecc 0.556 → 0.568, bearing 0.841 → 0.848, stem flexure 0.327 → 0.336, heel flexure 0.139 → 0.144; RIDOT sliding (construction stage governs) 1.172 → 1.223.

### ABC (c). Semi-integral: bearing shear from the movement on by default   [calc change, default] [MORE conservative]
- **Where:** select change handler (anchor `if(p==="iab.type"&&raw==="semi"&&S.longit&&!S.longit.computeTU)`), `migrate()` (anchor `pre=S.iab.diaRx===undefined`).
- **Before:** TU off unless turned on (the girder TU reactions of panel I-5 × the floating share). **After:** choosing semi-integral turns the TU calculation on (F = G·A·Δ/h_rt per bearing, 100 % share). A semi-integral project saved before this PR keeps its setting; a one-time notice says the default changed (saved data unchanged).
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.12.2, 14.6.3.1 (Eq. 14.6.3.1-2).

- **Where:** `computeIAB` (anchor `ABC (d), 2026-10-21: integral abutment, Extreme Event I`), dashboard `iabEEP`, `iabEEWF`, `iabEEWV`, `iabEERF`, `iabEERV`, Tab 10 §10.5d (`o-iab-ee`), K_PE input for integral (panel I-0a, seismic on), Tab 2 §2.1 text.

### ABC (decision 3). Integral attached wings: at-rest pressure and k_h = k_h0   [calc change] [MORE conservative]
- **Where:** `computeWing` (anchors `const itWing=att&&iabType()==="integral";`, `const kEff=itWing? "atrest"`, `khR=itWing? 1 : (+S.seismic.khR||0)`), Tab 9 §9.1 text (`ruleTxtI`), owner card (Kmode and khR rows no longer listed for integral).
- **Before:** the state and k_h came from the abutment's `fnd.branch` (spread by default): active K_a (AASHTO, RIDOT), Coulomb K_a by the MassDOT 3.1.6 "on soil" branch, and k_h = 0.5·k_h0 (MassDOT on spread). **After:** wing attached to an integral abutment: on piles → at-rest K₀ (MassDOT 3.1.6 and RIDOT 11.3.4 give K₀ for walls on piles; other owners AASHTO C3.11.1), γ_EH,max = 1.35 (at-rest), k_h = k_h0. CTDOT (already at-rest, case 1) unchanged. Semi-integral wings keep the lower abutment's foundation (its real foundation).
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 3.11.5.2, C3.11.1, Table 3.4.1-2, 11.6.5.2.2; MassDOT Part I 3.1.6; RIDOT BDM 11.3.4.

Junction before → after: AASHTO flexure 0.415 → 0.594, shear 0.138 → 0.235, min 0.552 → 0.693, crack 0.262 → 0.433; MassDOT 0.356 → 0.591, 0.100 → 0.210, 0.474 → 0.770, 0.222 → 0.432; RIDOT 0.415 → 0.594, 0.138 → 0.235, 0.552 → 0.693, 0.367 → 0.625; CTDOT unchanged.

### Tab 9 wording
- Attached wing "cast monolithic with the stem / backwall" → integral: "the integral wall (pile cap and end diaphragm), moving with it"; semi-integral: "the lower abutment (stem; the end diaphragm moves separately on the bearings)". §9.2a: resultants act on the "pile cap / integral wall" (integral) or "lower-abutment stem" (semi); integral: the pair weight goes to the integral piles (link §10.4).

### Saved data
- New key `iab.diaRx` (default false; additive). Old semi-integral saves: TU setting kept, one-time notice. Input ID of integral / semi-integral projects changes (new key). No other key or format changed.

### How verified
- `node tests/check-syntax.mjs`: all scripts pass.
- Playwright, origin/main `eac35f4` vs branch, 21 configurations (all types × four owners, conv/semi on piles, conv and integral with seismic, integral without wings, an old semi save, semi with diaRx). Conventional (6, incl. seismic and piles): `computeAll` identical. Hand checks above equal the tool. No console errors; all tabs and the report render.

### Open items
1. The integral approach-slab inertia (APS-7, `Q.apEE`) still uses the abutment k_h (0.5·k_h0 on the spread default); the new EE check uses k_h0. Harmonize?
2. Rigid-cap distribution of the wing pair to the piles (equal share); an end pile under a flexible cap takes more.
3. Wall panel inertia is in the driving force but not deducted from the panel load (small, conservative).

## 2026-10-21 — PR: claude/abut-handoffs-iab — Integral / semi-integral hand-offs: integral per-pile foundation loads, R_n / φ into the integral inputs, type-aware SubLoads import (AXI) (PR link added after merge)

Cross-tool connection in one PR (CLAUDE.md §7 exception): abutment_calculator.html (sender of foundationLoads, receiver of pileResults and abutmentLoads), Pile Designer.html and Spread Footing.html (receivers of foundationLoads), HANDOFF.md §4.5, §4.6, §4.10. Every code site is tagged `AXI`. **No calculation changes in any tool:** the abutment's `computeAll` is identical to origin/main (`c729c12`) for conventional, semi-integral and integral projects (with seismic, on piles); the receivers change only what they accept.

### AXI-1. foundationLoads for an integral abutment: per-pile cases and `element.type`   [hand-off; no result change]
- **Where:** `AbutFoundationHandoff`: new `integralCases(R,lsSel)` (anchor `function integralCases(R,lsSel){`), `build()` (anchors `const integ0=iabType()==="integral"&&R.iab&&R.iab.integ;`, `p.element.abutmentType=iabType();`, `p.element.type="integralAbutment";`), `integralBlock` gravity (anchor `DC:r3((Q.DC+(Q.Wwing||0))/P.n)`), dialog text.
- **Before:** an integral abutment sent the conventional cantilever cases (bottom of footing, footing centre, 23–27 cases with P ≈ 3 000 kip, active EH and BR / TU shares) with only a note that they were not part of the integral design; `integral.gravity.DC = Q.DC/n` (without the wing pair of ABC a).
- **After:** `element.type = "integralAbutment"`, `element.abutmentType = "integral"`, `reference = {level:"pileHead", point:"pile", perPile:true}`, `perPile:true`, no `geometry` (`geometryIntegral` instead), integral notes, and per-pile cases: Strength I P max (P_g; CTDOT P_u = P_g + R_T), Strength I P min, Extreme Event I P max (seismic on), Service I P max (factored:false), Vx = Vy = Mx = My = 0 (lateral demand = the imposed movement, `integral.thermal.delta`). `gravity.DC`, `gravity.DL` include the wing pair, so η(γDC·DC + γDW·DW + γLL·LL) = P_g. Conventional and semi-integral: only `element.abutmentType` added (content hash unchanged).
- **Check (integral AASHTO default, seismic on, 6 × HP12X84):** DC = 717.9, W_wing = 38.25, DW = 72.0, LL on the piles 340.0 kip; Strength I P max = P_g = 274.70 kip; P min = 121.22; Extreme Event I = (717.9 + 38.25 + 72.0)/6 + 0 × LL = 138.03 (γEQ = 0); Service I = (717.9 + 38.25 + 72.0)/6 + 340.0/6 = 138.03 + 56.67 = 194.69 kip (tool = hand). MassDOT: gravity DC = (790.5 + 38.25)/6 = 138.125, DW 13.76, LL 77.437 → Pile Designer's demand 1.25(138.125) + 1.50(13.76) + 1.75(77.437) = 328.81 kip = the abutment's P_g.

### AXI-2. pileResults: R_n / φ into the integral inputs   [hand-off]
- **Where:** `AbutPileResults` `defaults()` (anchor `return { geo:!!(g&&g.static), rn:`), `plan()` (anchor `const geoOn=st.geo&&g&&g.static&&(conv? pileB : iabType()==="integral"), kp=conv? "piles." : "iab.";`).
- **Before:** Pile Designer's geotechnical R_n / φ were imported only for a conventional / semi-integral abutment on piles; an integral abutment's warning pointed to Pile Designer but nothing mapped. **After:** for an integral abutment the static (or field-method) R_n, φ_c and the uplift R_n,up, φ_up go to `iab.Rn`, `iab.phiC`, `iab.RnUp`, `iab.phiUp` (panel I-0a; marked "PD", stale handling as PXR2). Checked: a payload with R_n = 520, φ = 0.55, R_n,up = 180, φ_up = 0.40 plans exactly those four inputs.

### AXI-3. abutmentLoads (SubLoads) import: type-aware   [hand-off]
- **Where:** receiver `check` (anchor `if(iabType()==="integral"){ const keep=["geom.Lab","geom.spanL","geom.skew","mat.gc"];`, `o.gerr.brg="integral abutment: no bearings`), `unused()`.
- **Before:** type-blind: an integral abutment was offered the stem / footing / backwall geometry, the elastomeric bearing pad, BR / TU / CR·SH and WS / WL. **After (integral):** geometry limited to L_ab, span, skew, γ_c (the rest listed as not used); bearing pad, BR, TU, CR/SH, WS, WL disabled with the reason; layout, DC, DW, LL+IM, A_s and ΔT apply. Conventional and semi-integral unchanged.

### Saved data
- No key or format changed. Payloads: additive (`element.abutmentType`); the integral payload's `cases`, `reference`, `location`, `includes` change (receivers updated in this PR; HANDOFF.md §4.6).

### How verified
- `node tests/check-syntax.mjs` on the three tools: all scripts pass.
- Playwright, origin/main vs branch: `computeAll` identical for conventional (spread, pile, seismic), semi-integral (spread, pile) and integral (MassDOT, CTDOT, AASHTO seismic). foundationLoads payload: conventional / semi-integral differ only by `element.abutmentType`; integral as AXI-1 (values above).
- One browser context: SubLoads "Send to Abutment Calculator" → abutment (integral) "Pull from SubLoads": the dialog disables bearing, BR, TU, CR/SH, WS, WL with the reason and offers L_ab, span, skew only in the geometry group. Pile Designer `PileFoundationXfer.check/plan` on the integral payload: default target "Integral-abutment mode", plan without error, gravity demand 328.811 = P_u 328.810; group target refused. Spread Footing `bxFl.check`: refused with the integral message. No page errors.

## 2026-10-21 — PR: claude/abut-ap-kh0 — Integral approach-slab inertia with k_h0 (ABK) (PR link added after merge)

### ABK-1. Integral abutment, Extreme Event I: approach-slab inertia with k_h = k_h0   [calc change, integral + approach slab + seismic only] [MORE conservative]
- **Where:** `computeIAB`, APS block (anchor `const kh=isFinite(R.seis.kh0)? R.seis.kh0 : R.seis.kh, W=AP.RDC+AP.RDW;`).
- **Before:** `const kh=R.seis.kh, W=AP.RDC+AP.RDW;` — the abutment k_h (k_h ratio of panel I-11 × k_h0; 0.5·k_h0 on the spread-footing default). **After:** `const kh=isFinite(R.seis.kh0)? R.seis.kh0 : R.seis.kh, W=AP.RDC+AP.RDW;` — k_h0, as the integral wall Extreme Event I check (§10.5d, ABC d) and the integral wings (ABC decision 3): the integral abutment is restrained by the superstructure and the piles, so the 11.6.5.2.2 displacement reduction does not apply. Engineer's decision 2026-10-21.
- **Provision:** AASHTO LRFD 10th Ed. 11.6.5.2.1, 11.6.5.2.2, 11.6.5.1; APS-7.
- **Check (integral, approach slab on, seismic on, A_s = 0.15, k_h ratio 0.5, R_DC + R_DW = 66.0 + 10.56 = 76.56 kip, F = 45.94 kip):** before F_EQ = min(0.075 × 76.56, 45.94) = 5.742 kip; after min(0.150 × 76.56, 45.94) = 11.484 kip. §10.5d: F_d 129.96 → 135.71 kip; MassDOT / RIDOT f = F_d/P_PE 0.1193 → 0.1246 (P_PE = 1089.3), wall case 2 M_u 4.201 → 4.386 kip-ft/ft (D/C 0.036 → 0.038); CTDOT (P_PE = 1403.3) 0.0926 → 0.0967.
